title:

We’re plan
title_en:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

https://t.co/vcaoHROTt2

full_text_en:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

https://t.co/vcaoHROTt2
full_text_zh:
随着人工智能发现漏洞的能力越来越强，防御者需要在攻击者之前将其投入使用。

我们正在计划 OpenAI 的下一次内部安全冲刺，并与 Cathedral Systems 合作，后者的研究人员将与我们的团队一起使用我们的模型来挑战我们的防御。他们将为我们正在进行的工作带来差异化的专业知识和方法，以发现并修复人工智能的弱点。

我们还提高了错误赏金奖励，其中对关键发现的奖励将增加四倍以上。杰出的发现将有资格获得高达 172,000 美元的奖金，包括奖金。

我们将不断改进我们的模型，利用它们来增强我们自己的系统，并扩大可信赖的防御者的访问范围。

title: If engineers push to different branches, Pando can update both in parallel. If we push to the same branch, it still puts
title_en:
If engineers push to different branches, Pando can update both in parallel. If we push to the same branch, it still puts those updates in order.

On a fetch, you get the history for each branch tip, but two tips may reflect different points in time. https://t.co/JhpglDvCa9
title_zh:
如果工程师推送到不同的分支，Pando 可以并行更新两个分支。如果我们推送到同一个分支，它仍然会按顺序排列这些更新。

在获取时，您可以获得每个分支提示的历史记录，但两个提示可能反映不同的时间点。

title:

First, the most important thing: WorkO
title_en:
I want to share some context on a security incident we discovered on October 30.

First, the most important thing: WorkOS's production systems are secure. No customer platform data was accessed. This incident was isolated to internal GTM systems.

The attack involved ARTEX, an autonomous AI agent framework used to carry out offensive security operations. It's a striking example of how quickly the capabilities of attackers are evolving.

We've contained the incident, brought in independent experts to investigate, and are working through the details.

Security is something we take extremely seriously, and I believe in being transparent when things go wrong. We'll continue to share updates as we learn more.

Full details: https://t.co/6Pt6Nt7kr5

full_text_zh:
我想分享一些我们 10 月 30 日发现的安全事件的背景信息。

首先，最重要的是：WorkOS 的生产系统是安全的。未访问任何客户平台数据。此事件与 GTM 内部系统无关。

此次攻击涉及 ARTEX，这是一个用于执行攻击性安全操作的自主人工智能代理框架。这是攻击者能力发展速度如此之快的一个引人注目的例子。

我们已经控制了这一事件，聘请了独立专家进行调查，并正在研究细节。

安全是我们非常重视的事情，我相信在出现问题时应该保持透明。当我们了解更多信息时，我们将继续分享更新。

title_en:

“With Siri AI, we really have the kind of the Siri that we always wanted. title: I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play h
title_en:
I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play here:

👉 https://t.co/6C8H8KtSaU 👈

(It's the free shareware demo)

It was way harder than the other ports like Quake and DOOM I did because they already had lots of open source projects and work behind them

In case of Battlefield 1942 there was literally absolutely nothing to work on top of, nobody had ever ported it and there was no open source engine for it, nor did the makers ever open source it (like id Software did with Quake 3)

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)

- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web

full_text_zh:
我反编译了可能是我最喜欢的游戏：《战地 1942》，并将其放在网上，提供多人游戏供您在这里玩：

👉 👈

（这是免费的共享软件演示）

这比我做的《Quake》和《DOOM》等其他移植要困难得多，因为他们已经有很多开源项目和背后的工作

就《战地 1942》而言，实际上完全没有任何东西可以在上面工作，没有人移植它，也没有开源引擎，制作者也没有开源它（就像 id Software 对《雷神之锤 3》所做的那样）

我在 6 个月前尝试过，essentiay 放弃了，但今天我再次尝试，Opus 5.5 询问“你可以尝试将此文件夹中的 BF1942 演示移植到网络吗”

所以我和 Claude Code（老实说，主要是 Claude Code）今天做了一些疯狂的事情：
- 它反汇编了 x86 原始机器代码以找到 57,000 个 x86 函数
- 它将每个 x86 函数转换为 C 函数（mov eax, [esi+0x110] 变为 eax = READ32(esi + 0x110)，顺便说一句，我不知道这意味着什么）
- 它输出了 100,000 行 C
- 然后使用 Emscripten 将其编译为 WebAsswmbly
- 使用了 300 个 Windows 和 Direct3D 函数，我们必须将其重写为 WebGL 2 和 OpenGL 才能在网络上工作
- 然后我们必须构建自己的网络堆栈，以便它可以通过 WebSocket 连接到我们的多人游戏服务器

我不知道它是如何做到这一点的，但它做到了，而且似乎有效！ 😊

来这里玩并报告任何错误！

title: $PLTR just delivered one of the most INSANE earnings reports I've seen from a software company, and these numbers are ab
title_en:
$PLTR just delivered one of the most INSANE earnings reports I've seen from a software company, and these numbers are absolutely ridiculous.

The company reported $2.31 BILLION in quarterly revenue, growing 96% year over year, while adjusted operating income reached $1.43 billion. But what really caught my attention was its Rule of 40 score, which just hit an unbelievable 158%. For those unfamiliar, the Rule of 40 combines a company's revenue growth rate with its operating margin to measure how efficiently it is growing. A score of 40% is generally considered healthy for a software company. Palantir just posted 158%, combining roughly 96% revenue growth with a 62% adjusted operating margin.

And what's even crazier is how quickly this has improved. Palantir's score was just 81% in Q4 2024, climbed to 114% by Q3 2025, and has now nearly doubled to 158% in less than two years. The biggest driver continues to be its U.S. commercial business, which grew an incredible 148% year over year to $984 million. U.S. commercial remaining deal value also increased 79% to $6.52 billion, while the company closed 64 deals worth at least $10 million during the quarter.

I think this tells us a lot about where enterprise AI adoption is heading. Companies are moving beyond experimenting with AI and increasingly deploying it across their actual operations. And Palantir is showing what happens when that adoption starts translating into massive revenue growth without requiring expenses to grow anywhere near as quickly. What makes these results even more impressive is that Palantir isn't sacrificing profitability to achieve this growth. Its software business is scaling incredibly efficiently, and that combination of accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins is something very few companies have been able to accomplish at this scale.

full_text_zh:
$PLTR 刚刚发布了我所见过的软件公司中最疯狂的收益报告之一，这些数字绝对是荒谬的。

该公司报告季度收入为 23.1 亿美元，同比增长 96%，调整后营业收入达到 14.3 亿美元。但真正引起我注意的是它的 40 规则得分，达到了令人难以置信的 158%。对于那些不熟悉的人来说，40 法则将公司的收入增长率与其营业利润率结合起来，以衡量其增长效率。对于软件公司来说，40% 的分数通常被认为是健康的。 Palantir 刚刚公布了 158% 的业绩，收入增长约 96%，调整后营业利润率为 62%。

更疯狂的是这种情况改善得有多快。 Palantir 的得分在 2024 年第四季度仅为 81%，到 2025 年第三季度攀升至 114%，现在在不到两年的时间里几乎翻了一番，达到 158%。最大的推动力仍然是其美国商业业务，该业务同比增长 148%，达到 9.84 亿美元。美国商业剩余交易价值也增长了 79%，达到 65.2 亿美元，而该公司在本季度完成了 64 笔价值至少 1000 万美元的交易。

我认为这告诉我们很多关于企业人工智能采用的走向。公司正在超越对人工智能的试验，并越来越多地将其部署到实际运营中。 Palantir 正在展示当这种采用开始转化为巨大的收入增长而不要求支出以同样快的速度增长时会发生什么。使这些结果更加令人印象深刻的是 Palantir 并没有牺牲盈利能力来实现这一增长。其软件业务正在以令人难以置信的效率扩展，而加速收入增长和扩大利润的结合是很少有公司能够实现如此规模的。

Imagine if everyone had the tools to shape intelligence itself. That day is today.

Today we launch the Trajectory platform - the easiest and most intuitive tool to post-train models of your own. The foundation for continual learning.

With just a few agent prompts, you get access to a full creative suite to train, eval, and deploy trillion parameter models.

title_en:
holy f*ck, someone just dropped an entire reverse engineering degree on GitHub for free.

Now you can build agents that can reverse engineer almost anything:

1. Ghidra  
How to read any binary.  
The NSA’s reverse engineering framework. Where almost everyone starts.  
https://t.co/0gMtMY4RCu

2. radare2  
The same skill, but in the terminal.  
UNIX-style reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset.  
https://t.co/9VSZmM7Jxz

3. LLM4Decompile  
An LLM that decompiles.  
Turns binary code into readable C. The 9B v2 model hits 64.9% re-executability on its own benchmark.  
https://t.co/eWiIpSSFF4

4. r2ai  
An LLM inside radare2.  
LLM-powered reversing for radare2. This is where AI starts reading the binary with you.  
https://t.co/pEYfM1bF7L

5. ida-pro-mcp  
Let the agent drive the tool.  
Bridges IDA Pro to language models through MCP.  
https://t.co/yog4GhEJ72

6. reverse-engineering-assistant  
The same thing for Ghidra.  
An MCP server for reverse engineering tasks inside Ghidra.  
https://t.co/4CYyNsMmel

7. REA  
Agents that reverse engineer anything.  
35 target types: native binaries, APKs, firmware, websites, Electron apps, and more. Every finding is backed by evidence.  
https://t.co/OfBDMN188q

full_text_zh:
天哪，有人刚刚在 GitHub 上免费发布了整个逆向工程学位。

现在您可以构建几乎可以对任何东西进行逆向工程的代理：

1.吉德拉
如何读取任何二进制文件。
美国国家安全局的逆向工程框架。几乎每个人都从这里开始。

2.雷达2
相同的技能，但在终端中。
UNIX 风格的逆向工程框架和命令行工具集。

3.LLM4反编译
反编译的法学硕士。
将二进制代码转换为可读的 C 代码。9B v2 模型在其自己的基准测试中达到了 64.9% 的可重复执行性。

4. r2ai
雷达雷2内部的法学硕士。
LLM 驱动的radare2 倒车。这是人工智能开始与您一起读取二进制文件的地方。

5. ida-pro-mcp
让代理驱动该工具。
通过 MCP 将 IDA Pro 连接到语言模型。

6. 逆向工程助手
对于吉德拉来说也是如此。
用于 Ghidra 内部逆向工程任务的 MCP 服务器。

7. 房地产
对任何东西进行逆向工程的代理。
35 种目标类型：本机二进制文件、APK、固件、网站、Electron 应用程序等。每项发现都有证据支持。

阅读下面完整的 REA 指南 ↓

title_en:
Shocking if true. Haiti, children and the Clinton Foundation…

Dave Collum’s theory is that some political decisions only make sense if something is hanging over the people making them. He calls it the gravitational force.

His case study is a 2010 Haiti child-smuggling arrest that ended with a time-served sentence. 

This is an interesting lens for looking at decisions that defy logic…whether or not you buy all the connections he draws…

如果属实就令人震惊。海地、儿童和克林顿基金会……

他的案例研究是 2010 年在海地逮捕的一起走私儿童案，最终被判服

title_en:
I genuinely don't understand why everyone isn't using this yet

With the help of this concept, my business reached an income of $13,000 per month

Andrej Karpathy noted: "The primary regret among engineers in my field right now is every AI conversation they failed to save. In 10 years, the people who started archiving in 2024 will leave the rest of us in the dust" 

co-founder of OpenAI, generated 25M views around a single concept: stop using AI just to code, and start using it to construct a second brain that remembers every article, PDF, transcript, and chat you have ever provided

You simply direct Claude Code to a folder, throw any file into it, and Claude scans the content, connects it to existing records, and builds a living wiki. Your personal knowledge finally stacks up like compound interest instead of slipping away every weekend

The stack:

> Brew install obsidian⁠, ⁠mkdir ~/vault⁠, ⁠cd ~/vault⁠
> Launch claude inside that directory and enter: "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
> Place any file into ⁠/raw⁠ (a YouTube transcript, meeting notes, a 400-page PDF, or a tweet screenshot) and enter "ingest"
> Claude constructs a wiki page, links it to 5 existing documents automatically, and updates ⁠CLAUDE.md⁠ with any fresh patterns it spots in your thinking style
> Never launch a blank Claude chat window again. Every prompt runs through your vault, and every reply cites your own materials with dates and links

It takes 5 minutes to set up, letting your knowledge compound from that night onward

The harsh truth most people will scroll past: in 10 years, the engineers who adopted this in 2024 will recall every book, podcast, and meeting with solid proof. You will remember virtually nothing. Karpathy has already made his decision, and you are still falling behind

Check the article below for the complete step-by-step walkthrough

Save this to your bookmarks before you waste another Monday

title: Anthropic has updated Claude Code to stop it from recreating existing video games. The change was first spotted by X use
title_en:
Anthropic has updated Claude Code to stop it from recreating existing video games. The change was first spotted by X user Chasm on October 27 and confirmed by Anthropic's Addy Osmani on October 30.
 
According to the initial report from Tom's Hardware, original games and genre-based projects are still allowed. However, some developers report that Claude is now also blocking legitimate tasks like debugging and reverse engineering.

title:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’
title_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!
title_zh:
今天我宣布 Workers IO 来解决工程中最慢的部分——验证！

人工智能代理现在可以在几天内编写出多年的代码，但仍然需要大量的工程工作来验证正在构建的内容。

不可能预测所有可能导致故障的情况，这就是为什么最昂贵的故障出现在生产中。

title:
This is captain Francesco Schettino, very popular in the maritime industry, but for the wrong reason.

Sentenced to Sixt
title_en:
This is captain Francesco Schettino, very popular in the maritime industry, but for the wrong reason.

Sentenced to Sixteen years in prison for manslaughter, causing a shipwreck, and abandoning his post.

Here’s what happened. 

On January 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia ran aground off the coast of Giglio, Italy. What followed became one of the most disgraceful maritime disasters in modern passenger shipping, not because of a storm, structural fault, or mechanical blackout, but because of gross command failure.

The vessel was executing a routine Mediterranean passage when Schettino authorized an unscheduled deviation to sail extraordinarily close to the island for a visual "salute." It was a reckless stunt that had zero navigational necessity. At high speed, the ship struck a submerged reef, ripping a massive breach along the port hull.

Following the impact, main electrical power failed and rapid flooding began. Instead of sounding emergency stations and executing an immediate evacuation, the bridge actively concealed the reality. Passengers were informed that the vessel was merely suffering a minor technical malfunction and were instructed to remain in their cabins. That delay proved fatal.

As progressive flooding destabilized the vessel, she took on a heavy list, rendering half the survival craft useless. By the time the general emergency order was given, chaos had overtaken the decks. Passengers were left fighting through listing corridors, with several forced straight into the water.

Then came the ultimate breach of command trust: Captain Schettino abandoned the vessel while hundreds of passengers and crew were still trapped onboard. Official radio transcripts later captured maritime authorities ordering him to return to his ship, an order he ignored.
32 people died. The Costa Concordia sat partially submerged on the rocks of Giglio for over two years before undergoing one of the most expensive salvage operations in history to be refloated and scrapped.

Today, the Costa Concordia is a standard case study in maritime academies worldwide on bridge resource management breakdown, total leadership collapse, and the catastrophic consequences of ignoring safety protocols. It remains a grim reminder that at sea, major disasters rarely start with a mechanical failure; they start with poor choices made on the bridge long before the water ever comes in.

因过失杀人、造成海难、弃职等罪被判处十六年有期徒刑。

这就是发生的事情。

2012年1月13日，歌诗达协和号在意大利

full_text_zh:
这位船长是弗朗西斯科·谢蒂诺 (Francesco Schettino)，他在航海业中非常受欢迎，但原因却是错误的。

因过失杀人、造成海难、弃职等罪被判处十六年有期徒刑。

这就是发生的事情。

2012年1月13日，歌诗达协和号在意大利吉利奥海岸搁浅。接下来发生的事情成为现代客运中最可耻的海上灾难之一，不是因为风暴、结构故障或机械停电，而是因为严重的指挥失误。

当斯凯蒂诺授权计划外偏离该船时，该船正在执行地中海例行航行，非常靠近该岛航行，以进行视觉“敬礼”。这是一个鲁莽的特技，导航必要性为零。这艘船高速行驶时撞上了水下的礁石，在港口船体上撕开了一个巨大的缺口。

撞击发生后，主电源发生故障，洪水开始迅速蔓延。大桥没有拉响应急站并立即实施疏散，而是主动隐瞒事实。乘客被告知，该船只是遭遇了轻微的技术故障，并被指示留在自己的船舱内。事实证明，这一延误是致命的。

随着洪水的不断蔓延，船只变得不稳定，她的船体严重倾斜，导致一半的救生艇无法使用。当总体紧急命令下达时，甲板上已经一片混乱。乘客们在倾斜的走廊里打斗，有几人直接被推入水中。

随后，最终出现了违反指挥信任的情况：谢蒂诺船长弃船而去，而数百名乘客和船员仍被困在船上。官方无线电记录后来捕捉到海事当局命令他返回船上的消息，但他无视了这一命令。
32人死亡。歌诗达康科迪亚号部分淹没在吉利奥的岩石上两年多，然后进行了历史上最昂贵的打捞作业之一，重新浮起并报废。

如今，歌诗达协和号已成为全球海事院校研究桥梁资源管理崩溃、领导层全面崩溃以及忽视安全协议所造成的灾难性后果的标准案例。这仍然是一个严峻的提醒：在海上，重大灾难很少是由机械故障开始的。早在水进来之前，他们就在桥上做出了错误的选择。

title:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The app
title_en:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The approach used several model providers at once: an in-house assistant built on models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet, plus Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub for bankers who wanted to build their own tools

As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by traders and bankers, who built tools with AI and passed them to engineers to finish

In October, Goldman reversed course. Per reporting from Bloomberg, updated internal guidance now limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers after a review of productivity and risk, and some traders are frustrated

A week before the story ran, Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO with Goldman as one of two lead underwriters

Here are the five moves that took Goldman from vibe coding to engineers only

1. GS AI Assistant

In June 2025, Goldman took its internal chatbot firmwide after a pilot with about 10,000 users, out of a workforce of roughly 46,500

The assistant runs inside Goldman's compliance perimeter and gives staff access to models including ChatGPT and Gemini

Argenti rolled out GitHub Copilot and Gemini Code Assist, and Goldman became the first major bank to use Cognition's autonomous coding agent, Devin

By August 2026, hundreds of Devin agents were working alongside roughly 12,000 human developers, and Argenti said the deployment could grow into the thousands

2. Claude in the back office

In February, Argenti told CNBC that Anthropic engineers had been embedded inside Goldman for six months, building autonomous agents on Claude

The first targets were trade and transaction accounting and client vetting and onboarding. 

3. Hong Kong

In late April, the Financial Times reported that Goldman had cut off Anthropic's models for its Hong Kong bankers
Staff there had used Claude through the bank's internal AI platform and had lost access in the preceding weeks

The FT said the cause was a strict reading of Goldman's contract with Anthropic, made after consulting the company. 

Anthropic told the FT that Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong
Gemini and ChatGPT stayed on the platform, so the restriction applied to Claude only and was not a ban on AI

4. Nvidia and Anthropic

While the internal rules were tightening, Goldman's AI banking business was growing

It is underwriting Anthropic's IPO and helping Nvidia arrange large debt deals

In August, Nvidia signed memoranda of understanding with KKR, Goldman, Brookfield, Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo to set up compute financing platforms

The goal is to bring in more than $500 billion of outside capital over time. Solomon has said Jensen Huang brought the idea to Goldman

On October 26, Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters
IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

5. Engineers only

The October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers. Strats, who work across trading, quant research and engineering, are exempt

Traders had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and produce written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg

A Goldman spokesperson said the bank makes AI tools available across the firm to find use cases

After a trial period weighing productivity and risk, it gives them to the people best placed to use them long term

Bloomberg noted that banks are spending millions of dollars on AI tools while also managing cybersecurity risk, cost and productivity

Non-engineers who relied on Claude Code or GitHub now need to request other tools or use the GS AI Assistant instead

That leaves Claude Code with roughly 26% of Goldman's headcoun

高盛花了两年时间向其约 46,000 名员工推广人工智能，而不仅仅是其 12,000 名工程师

该方法同时使用了多个模型提供商：一个基于 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Alphabet 的模型构建的内部助手，以及 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和 Microsoft 的 GitHub，供想要构建自己的工具的银行家使用

就在 7 月，首席信息官 Marco Argenti 还在推广交易员和银行家的“vibe 编码”，他们用人工智能构建工具并将其传递给工程师来完成

十月，高盛改变了方针。根据彭博社的报道，在对生产力和风险进行审查后，更新后的内部指南现在将 Claude Code 和 GitHub 限制为工程师使用，一些交易者感到沮丧

报道发布前一周，Anthropic 作为两家主承销商之一向高盛公开申请 IPO

以下是高盛从氛围编码转变为工程师的五个举措

1.GS人工智能助手

2025 年 6 月，高盛在约 46,500 名员工中进行了约 10,000 名用户试点后，在全公司范围内采用了内部聊天机器人

该助手在高盛的合规范围内运行，让员工可以访问包括 ChatGPT 和 Gemini 在内的模型

Argenti 推出了 GitHub Copilot 和 Gemini Code Assist，高盛成为第一家使用 Cognition 自主编码代理 Devin 的大型银行

到 2026 年 8 月，数百名 Devin 代理与大约 12,000 名人类开发人员一起工作，Argenti 表示部署数量可能会增加到数千人

2.克劳德在后台

今年 2 月，Argenti 告诉 CNBC，Anthropic 工程师已在高盛内部工作了六个月，在 Claude 上构建了自主代理

第一个目标是贸易和交易会计以及客户审查和入职。

3. 香港

4月下旬，英国《金融时报》报道称，高盛已切断其香港银行家的Anthropic模型
那里的工作人员通过银行的内部人工智能平台使用了克劳德，但在前几周失去了访问权限

英国《金融时报》表示，原因是高盛在咨询了 Anthropic 后，严格解读了该公司与该公司签订的合同。

Anthropic告诉英国《金融时报》，克劳德从未在香港得到正式支持
Gemini 和 ChatGPT 留在平台上，因此该限制仅适用于 Claude，并不是对 AI 的禁令

4. Nvidia 和 Anthropic

内部规则收紧的同时，高盛的AI银行业务却在增长

它正在承销 Anthropic 的 IPO 并帮助 Nvidia 安排大型债务交易

8 月，Nvidia 与 KKR、高盛、Brookfield、Blackstone、BlackRock 和 Apollo 签署谅解备忘录，建立计算融资平台

目标是随着时间的推移引入超过 5000 亿美元的外部资本。所罗门表示，黄仁勋将这个想法带给了高盛

10月26日，Anthropic申请在纳斯达克以ANT名义上市，高盛和摩根士丹利担任主承销商
IFR 报告称，此次发行可能通过 20 多家银行组成的银团筹集 750 亿至 1000 亿美元的资金

5.仅限工程师

10 月份的指南将 Claude Code 和 GitHub 限制为工程师使用。从事交易、量化研究和工程工作的 Strats 可以豁免

彭博社援引一位知情人士的话说，交易员一直在使用这些工具来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势和头寸，并生成书面和图形内容。

高盛发言人表示，该银行在整个公司范围内提供人工智能工具来寻找用例

经过一段权衡生产力和风险的试用期后，它会将它们提供给最适合长期使用它们的人

彭博社指出，银行在人工智能工具上花费了数百万美元，同时还管理网络安全风险、成本和生产力

依赖 Claude Code 或 GitHub 的非工程师现在需要请求其他工具或使用 GS AI Assistant

这样一来，Claude Code 就只剩下高盛大约 26% 的员工了

title:
Goldman Sachs just gave the AI industry a reality check.

After months of allowing bankers and traders to experiment wit
title_en:
Goldman Sachs just gave the AI industry a reality check.

After months of allowing bankers and traders to experiment with advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic’s Claude Code and Microsoft’s GitHub tools, Goldman is tightening access.

The new October guidance largely restricts these tools to engineers. Quantitative specialists, known as strats, are among those who retain access.

Why does this matter?

Traders had been using AI coding agents to monitor client trading flows, model market movements, analyze positions, and generate written and visual materials.

In other words, people who don’t traditionally write software were starting to build their own tools.

Some weren’t happy when access was restricted.

Goldman’s explanation was straightforward. The firm had completed an experimentation period and was evaluating productivity alongside risk management. It now wants these tools in the hands of people best equipped to use them over the long term.

But here’s where the story gets interesting.

Goldman isn’t abandoning AI.

Its internal GS AI Assistant is reportedly being used weekly by approximately 40,000 of its 46,200 employees.

The firm has also reported productivity improvements of at least 20% among its roughly 12,000 engineers using AI coding tools.

CIO Marco Argenti had even praised nontechnical employees experimenting with so-called vibe coding earlier this year.

Now the firm is pulling back on access to some of those same tools.

There is a bigger lesson here for the AI industry.

Getting employees to experiment with AI is relatively easy.

Turning experimentation into reliable production software is a different problem.

Banks have proprietary data, regulatory obligations, compliance requirements, cybersecurity risks, and accountability standards. A coding agent that works brilliantly in a demonstration still has to survive those realities.

And there’s another question.

If traders and bankers can use AI to build tools that previously required engineers, where does that leave the traditional technology department?

Goldman appears to be drawing a line between experimentation and production.

That may be a sensible decision.

But it also exposes the gap between what AI vendors promise and what large institutions are actually comfortable deploying.

The AI revolution isn’t being stopped. It’s being given a risk committee, an approval process, and restricted access.

Welcome to Wall Street.

Banks have proprietary data, regulatory obligations, compliance requirements, cybersecurity risks, and accountability standards. A coding agent that works brilliantly in a demonstration still has to survive those realities.

And there’s another question.

If traders and bankers can use AI to build tools that previously required engineers, where does that leave the traditional technology department?

Goldman appears to be drawing a line between experimentation and production.

That may be a sensible decision.

But it also exposes the gap between what AI vendors promise and what large institutions are actually comfortable deploying.

The AI revolution isn’t being stopped. It’s being given a risk committee, an approval process, and restricted access.

Welcome to Wall Street.
full_text_zh:
高盛刚刚对人工智能行业进行了现实检验。

在允许银行家和交易员尝试先进的人工智能编码工具（包括 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和微软的 GitHub 工具）几个月后，高盛正在收紧准入。

十月份的新指南很大程度上将这些工具限制为工程师使用。被称为 strats 的定量专家是保留访问权的人之一。

为什么这很重要？

交易员一直在使用人工智能编码代理来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势、分析头寸并生成书面和视觉材料。

换句话说，传统上不编写软件的人们开始构建自己的工具。

有些人对访问受到限制感到不满。

高盛的解释很简单。该公司已经完成了一个试验期，正在评估生产力和风险管理。现在，它希望这些工具掌握在最有能力长期使用它们的人手中。

但这就是故事变得有趣的地方。

高盛并没有放弃人工智能。

据报道，其 46,200 名员工中约有 40,000 人每周使用其内部 GS AI Assistant。

该公司还报告称，使用 AI 编码工具的约 12,000 名工程师的生产力提高了至少 20%。

首席信息官 Marco Argenti 甚至赞扬了今年早些时候尝试所谓的氛围编码的非技术员工。

现在，该公司正在取消对其中一些相同工具的访问。

对于人工智能行业来说，这里有一个更大的教训。

让员工尝试人工智能相对容易。

将实验转化为可靠的生产软件是另一个问题。

银行拥有专有数据、监管义务、合规要求、网络安全风险和问责标准。在演示中表现出色的编码代理仍然必须经受这些现实。

还有一个问题。

如果交易员和银行家可以使用人工智能来构建以前需要工程师才能完成的工具，那么传统技术部门将何去何从？

高盛似乎正在实验和生产之间划清界限。

这可能是一个明智的决定。

但这也暴露了人工智能供应商的承诺与大型机构实际愿意部署的之间的差距。

人工智能革命并未停止。它被赋予了一个风险委员会、一个审批流程和有限的访问权限。

欢迎来到华尔街。

title:
There's a bigger difference between an instruction and an objective than it first appears.

An instruction tells a syste
title_en:
There's a bigger difference between an instruction and an objective than it first appears.

An instruction tells a system exactly what to do.

An objective tells a system what you're trying to achieve.

That distinction seems small until you start thinking about autonomous AI agents.

If I tell a piece of software:

"Buy this asset."

There isn't much interpretation involved.

I've already made the decision.

The software simply carries it out.

But imagine I say:

"Here is the outcome I'm trying to achieve. Here are the boundaries you must respect. Figure out the appropriate actions."

Now we've entered completely different territory.

The human is no longer providing every step.

The human is providing direction.

That's one of the ideas behind @meetmotes that I keep coming back to.

The phrase "give your NFT an objective" sounds simple, but underneath it is an interesting question about how we may interact with software in the future.

For decades, our relationship with computers has largely been command-driven.

Click this.

Open that.

Move this file.

Execute this transaction.

Buy this asset.

Sell that asset.

Every action begins with a relatively specific human instruction.

AI agents introduce the possibility of changing that relationship.

Instead of continuously telling software what action to perform next, we could increasingly define what we're trying to accomplish and allow the system to determine how to work towards it within established boundaries.

That's not merely automation.

It's delegation.

And delegation requires a very different kind of relationship between the person setting the objective and the system attempting to fulfil it.

Think about the difference in everyday life.

If I give someone a list containing twenty individual tasks, I'm managing the process.

If I explain the outcome I need, establish the boundaries and allow that person to determine the best approach, I'm delegating responsibility.

Both can lead to the same destination.

But the amount of judgement required along the way is completely different.

That's what makes objective-driven AI agents interesting to me.

The value isn't necessarily that the human disappears from the process.

The human's role changes.

Instead of deciding every individual action, the human becomes responsible for defining the destination and determining the boundaries around the journey.

And honestly, I think defining a good objective might eventually prove harder than people expect.

"Make money" is technically an objective.

It's also a terrible one.

How much risk is acceptable?

Over what kind of conditions?

Using what capital?

Across which markets?

What behaviour is off-limits?

When should the agent stop pursuing the objective entirely?

Suddenly, the quality of the outcome depends heavily on the quality of the objective.

That raises an interesting possibility.

As autonomous agents become more capable, perhaps one of the valuable human skills won't be knowing how to perform every action ourselves.

It will be knowing how to define what success actually means.

Because intelligence can help find a route.

It cannot decide what destination matters to you unless you've communicated that clearly.

This becomes particularly interesting when combined with digital ownership.

An NFT has traditionally been something you possess.

Connecting an NFT with an AI agent and then giving that agent an objective introduces another layer entirely.

The asset isn't simply representing ownership anymore.

There's now a relationship between:

ownership

intent

rules

action

The owner establishes intent.

The boundaries establish what is acceptable.

The agent determines actions within those conditions.

And the objective ties everything together.

I don't think this means humans eventually hand over financial decision-making and walk away.

If anything, it could make human judgement more important in a different place.

We spend less time asking:

@meetmotes

full_text_zh:
指令和目标之间的差异比乍看起来更大。

指令准确地告诉系统要做什么。

目标告诉系统您想要实现的目标。

如果我告诉一个软件：

“购买该资产。”

没有太多解释。

我已经做出决定了。

软件只是简单地执行它。

但想象一下我说：

“这是我想要实现的结果。这是你必须尊重的界限。找出适当的行动。”

现在我们进入了完全不同的领域。

人类不再提供每一步。

人类正在提供方向。

这是我不断回顾的@meetmotes 背后的想法之一。

“给你的 NFT 一个目标”这句话听起来很简单，但背后隐藏着一个有趣的问题，即我们未来如何与软件交互。

几十年来，我们与计算机的关系很大程度上是命令驱动的。

单击此。

打开那个。

移动这个文件。

执行此交易。

购买该资产。

出售该资产。

每个动作都始于相对具体的人类指令。

人工智能代理引入了改变这种关系的可能性。

我们可以越来越多地定义我们想要完成的任务，并允许系统确定如何在既定的边界内实现目标，而不是不断地告诉软件下一步要执行什么操作。

这不仅仅是自动化。

这是代表团。

授权要求设定目标的人和试图实现目标的系统之间存在一种非常不同的关系。

想想日常生活中的差异。

如果我给某人一个包含二十个单独任务的列表，那么我正在管理该流程。

如果我解释我需要的结果，建立界限并允许那个人确定最佳方法，我就是在委派责任。

两者都可以通向同一个目的地。

但一路上所需的判断量却完全不同。

这就是我对目标驱动的人工智能代理感兴趣的原因。

其价值并不一定是人类从这个过程中消失。

人类的角色发生了变化。

人类不再决定每一个单独的行动，而是负责定义目的地并确定旅程的边界。

老实说，我认为定义一个好的目标最终可能会比人们预期的更困难。

“赚钱”在技术上是一个目标。

这也是一件可怕的事。

可接受的风险有多大？

需要什么样的条件？

用什么资本？

跨越哪些市场？

哪些行为是被禁止的？

代理人什么时候应该完全停止追求目标？

突然之间，结果的质量在很大程度上取决于目标的质量。

这就提出了一个有趣的可能性。

随着自主代理变得更加有能力，也许有价值的人类技能之一将不再是知道如何自己执行每项行动。

它将知道如何定义成功的真正含义。

因为情报可以帮助找到路线。

除非您清楚地传达了这一点，否则它无法决定哪个目的地对您来说很重要。

当与数字所有权相结合时，这变得特别有趣。

NFT 传统上是你所拥有的东西。

将 NFT 与 AI 代理连接起来，然后为该代理提供一个目标，这完全引入了另一层。

资产不再仅仅代表所有权。

现在之间存在关系：

所有权

意图

规则

行动

业主确定意图。

界限决定了什么是可以接受的。

代理决定在这些条件下的操作。

目标将一切联系在一起。

我不认为这意味着人类最终会放弃财务决策权并走开。

如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它可能会让人类的判断在不同的地方变得更加重要。

我们花更少的时间问：

@meetmotes

“给你的 NFT 一个目标”这句话听起来很简单，但背后隐藏着一个有趣的问题，即我们未来如何与软件交互。

几十年来，我们与计算机的关系很大程度上是命令驱动的。

单击此。

打开那个。

移动这个文件。

执行此交易。

购买该资产。

出售该资产。

每个动作都始于相对具体的人类指令。

人工智能代理引入了改变这种关系的可能性。

我们可以越来越多地定义我们想要完成的任务，并允许系统确定如何在既定的边界内实现目标，而不是不断地告诉软件下一步要执行什么操作。

这不仅仅是自动化。

这是代表团。

授权要求设定目标的人和试图实现目标的系统之间存在一种非常不同的关系。

想想日常生活中的差异。

如果我给某人一个包含二十个单独任务的列表，那么我正在管理该流程。

如果我解释我需要的结果，建立界限并允许那个人确定最佳方法，我就是在委派责任。

两者都可以通向同一个目的地。

但一路上所需的判断量却完全不同。

这就是我对目标驱动的人工智能代理感兴趣的原因。

价值并不一定是人类从这个过程中消失。

人类的角色发生了变化。

人类不再决定每一个单独的行动，而是负责定义目的地并确定旅程的边界。

老实说，我认为定义一个好的目标最终可能会比人们预期的更困难。

“赚钱”在技术上是一个目标。

这也是一件可怕的事。

可接受的风险有多大？

需要什么样的条件？

用什么资本？

跨越哪些市场？

哪些行为是被禁止的？

代理人什么时候应该完全停止追求目标？

突然之间，结果的质量在很大程度上取决于目标的质量。

这就提出了一个有趣的可能性。

随着自主代理变得更加有能力，也许有价值的人类技能之一将不再是知道如何自己执行每项行动。

它将知道如何定义成功的实际含义。

因为情报可以帮助找到路线。

除非您清楚地传达了这一点，否则它无法决定哪个目的地对您来说很重要。

当与数字所有权相结合时，这变得特别有趣。

NFT 传统上是你所拥有的东西。

将 NFT 与 AI 代理连接起来，然后为该代理提供一个目标，这完全引入了另一层。

资产不再仅仅代表所有权。

现在之间存在关系：

所有权

意图

规则

行动

业主确定意图。

界限决定了什么是可以接受的。

代理决定在这些条件下的操作。

目标将一切联系在一起。

我不认为这意味着人类最终会放弃财务决策权并走开。

如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它可能会让人类的判断在不同的地方变得更加重要。

我们花更少的时间问：

@meetmotes

title: I built more 3-statement models by hand at Morgan Stanley than I'd like to admit. Claude in Excel is a game changer ....
title_en:
I built more 3-statement models by hand at Morgan Stanley than I'd like to admit. Claude in Excel is a game changer .... here's how I build any model in 5 passes:

The process is all about context window management to minimize hardcodes + hallucinations and maximize control over model style.

(1) Gather the sources. Filings, earnings transcripts, raw financials and any model or template I already have. I have it make a clean folder I point Claude to.

(2) Turn the sources into a JSON or .md input. A short inputs file with historicals, segment KPIs, accounting definitions and operating drivers. This step converts many megabites of PDF's into a liteweight doc for RAG.

(3) Build the structure (in your firm style). Building the shell lets you reverse engineer your firm model style .... which Claude will never have context for.

(4) Add the forecast. I take the same historicals JSON or .md and run a deep research workflow to fill in those parameters but for forward assumptions. Obviously with sources so I can check assumptions. Then I layer in that file to project out forward assumptions.

(5) Audit it in a fresh chat. New chat is necessary to hard reset the context window (improves quality). A simple prompt even to check for hard + soft errors can rank issues by severity (eg broken formulas and things that don't tie to assumptions that look off)

If you're really advanced at Claude Code - you can wrap this into a programmatic skill package in your firm build style .... maybe I write a thread about that next time.

In the meantime, I've put together this AI for Excel build guide here: https://t.co/NGtAgScJSW

full_text_zh:
我在摩根士丹利手工构建的三语句模型比我愿意承认的还要多。 Excel 中的 Claude 是一个游戏规则改变者......以下是我如何通过 5 遍构建任何模型：

该过程都是关于上下文窗口管理，以最大限度地减少硬编码和幻觉并最大限度地控制模型样式。

(1) 收集来源。文件、收益记录、原始财务数据以及我已有的任何模型或模板。我让它创建了一个干净的文件夹，我指向克劳德。

(2) 将源转换为 JSON 或 .md 输入。包含历史记录、部门 KPI、会计定义和运营驱动因素的简短输入文件。此步骤将许多兆字节的 PDF 转换为 RAG 的轻量级文档。

(3) 构建结构（以您公司的风格）。构建外壳可以让你对你的公司模型风格进行逆向工程......克劳德永远不会有上下文。

(4)添加预测。我采用相同的历史 JSON 或 .md 并运行深入的研究工作流程来填充这些参数，但用于前瞻性假设。显然有来源，所以我可以检查假设。然后我将该文件分层以预测未来的假设。

(5) 在新的聊天中审核它。新的聊天对于硬重置上下文窗口（提高质量）是必要的。一个简单的提示，甚至检查硬错误和软错误都可以按严重程度对问题进行排名（例如，损坏的公式和与看似不合理的假设无关的事情）

如果你真的很擅长 Claude Code - 你可以将其包装到你公司构建风格的编程技能包中......也许我下次会写一个关于这个的主题。

与此同时，我在这里整理了这个 AI for Excel 构建指南：

When Neil Druckmann was handed the reigns of Uncharted 4 after Amy Hennig's departure he essentially looked at everything that had already been created and came up with the story within a couple of weeks. That's nuts!!

To take a game that was already in production and look at the existing art and design and create a story to fit within that mould in a few weeks is pretty incredible.

title:
Anything that holds money draws attackers who don't mind trying again.

I learned that the expensive way. I read on X th
title_en:
Anything that holds money draws attackers who don't mind trying again.

I learned that the expensive way. I read on X that the Ostium vault I was in had been hacked, opened my wallet, and about $2,000 was gone.

AI agents with wallets have it worse, because the attacker only has to send them words. The trick has a name, prompt injection: an order slipped into ordinary text that the AI then follows.

In May 2026 one of those orders came disguised as Morse code, and around $200,000 left an agent's wallet.

As an engineer, I know a setup that stays the same every time will eventually show its weak spot to someone who keeps trying. That agent had one filter and one model, unchanged on every try.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing takes that sameness away. Its validators are the separate reviewers that run the network.

Before any AI reads your text, each one reworks it in its own hidden way, with its own model. What fools one of them looks like nonsense to everyone else, and the majority overrules any one that slips.

Every try now lands on a reader the attacker has never seen.

Would you let an AI agent hold your money today, or only once it works like this?
title_zh:
任何能存钱的东西都会吸引不介意再次尝试的攻击者。

我以昂贵的方式了解到了这一点。我在 X 上看到我所在的 Ostium 金库被黑客入侵，打开我的钱包，大约 2,000 美元不见了。

拥有钱包的人工智能代理的情况更糟，因为攻击者只需向他们
full_text_en:
Anything that holds money draws attackers who don't mind trying again.

I learned that the expensive way. I read on X that the Ostium vault I was in had been hacked, opened my wallet, and about $2,000 was gone.

AI agents with wallets have it worse, because the attacker only has to send them words. The trick has a name, prompt injection: an order slipped into ordinary text that the AI then follows.

In May 2026 one of those orders came disguised as Morse code, and around $200,000 left an agent's wallet.

As an engineer, I know a setup that stays the same every time will eventually show its weak spot to someone who keeps trying. That agent had one filter and one model, unchanged on every try.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing takes that sameness away. Its validators are the separate reviewers that run the network.

Before any AI reads your text, each one reworks it in its own hidden way, with its own model. What fools one of them looks like nonsense to everyone else, and the majority overrules any one that slips.

Every try now lands on a reader the attacker has never seen.

Would you let an AI agent hold your money today, or only once it works like this?
full_text_zh:
任何能存钱的东西都会吸引不介意再次尝试的攻击者。

我以昂贵的方式了解到了这一点。我在 X 上看到我所在的 Ostium 金库被黑客入侵，打开我的钱包，大约 2,000 美元不见了。

拥有钱包的人工智能代理的情况更糟，因为攻击者只需向他们发送文字。这个技巧有一个名字，即提示注入：将命令滑入普通文本中，然后人工智能遵循。

2026 年 5 月，其中一份订单伪装成摩尔斯电码，一名特工的钱包里留下了约 20 万美元。

作为一名工程师，我知道每次都保持不变的设置最终会向不断尝试的人展示其弱点。该代理有一个过滤器和一个模型，每次尝试都没有改变。

@GenLayer 的灰盒消除了这种千篇一律。它的验证者是运行网络的独立审查者。

在任何人工智能阅读你的文本之前，每个人工智能都会用自己的模型以自己隐藏的方式对其进行修改。愚弄他们中的一个人的事情在其他人看来都是无稽之谈，而大多数人都会否决任何一个失误的事情。

现在，每次尝试都会落在攻击者从未见过的读者身上。

你会让人工智能代理今天保管你的钱，还是只在它像这样工作时才保管你的钱？

title: 412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. m
title_en:
412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. meet the Halcyon HX-7, a new orbital freighter prototype that only exists as a simulator

I built it with Elvar's teardown method. one free Claude Code skill, the whole ship in one offline HTML page

the whole mission is one timeline. 9 phases: approach, hold, gear down, cargo open, mast up, optics scan, teardown, reassembly, ascent burn. every panel reads that timeline. the main drive sits at 86 kN on approach, drops to 13 kN while the hull is apart and climbs to 89 kN on the ascent burn. the moment the sections split, all 8 load bars flip to DETACHED. the gauges follow the model, so they can't show a number the ship isn't living through

here is the gist:

→ type /teardown, name the vehicle, attach one real reference. without it you get a toy
→ write the mission as a timeline before any part gets a shape: 9 phases, each with a start time
→ split the hull into sections you can pull out alone: drive, aft, mid, fwd, nose, pod, mast, gear
→ give every phase real numbers: thrust in kN, altitude, velocity, which subsystem is live
→ point every panel at the timeline, never at its own animation
→ blow the hull apart mid-mission and check that every bar says DETACHED
→ dock it back and fire the burn. if one section comes home late, the numbers show it before your eyes do

a ship you can open, cut and fly says more than a render deck

the 9 prompts are in the quoted article

nose iris opening in orbit or 4 legs coming down at 7.69 km/s, which part of your own ship would you cut open first?

→ split the hull into sections you can pull out alone: drive, aft, mid, fwd, nose, pod, mast, gear
→ give every phase real numbers: thrust in kN, altitude, velocity, which subsystem is live
→ point every panel at the timeline, never at its own animation
→ blow the hull apart mid-mission and check that every bar says DETACHED
→ dock it back and fire the burn. if one section comes home late, the numbers show it before your eyes do

a ship you can open, cut and fly says more than a render deck

the 9 prompts are in the quoted article

nose iris opening in orbit or 4 legs coming down at 7.69 km/s, which part of your own ship would you cut open first?

↳ concept simulation, method from the article
full_text_zh:
海拔412公里。 7.69 公里/秒。 3 个发动机罩、4 个着陆腿、8 个船体部分，它们在轨道上分开并重新对接在一起。认识 Halcyon HX-7，一种仅作为模拟器存在的新型轨道货机原型

我用 Elvar 的拆解方法构建了它。一项免费的 Claude Code 技能，整艘船都在一个离线 HTML 页面中

整个任务就是一条时间线。 9 个阶段：进场、等待、起落架放下、货物打开、桅杆升起、光学扫描、拆卸、重新组装、上升燃烧。每个小组都会阅读该时间表。主驱动装置在接近时为 86 kN，在船体分离时降至 13 kN，在上升燃烧时升至 89 kN。当部分分裂时，所有 8 个负载杆都会翻转为分离状态。仪表遵循模型，因此它们无法显示船舶未经历过的数字

要点如下：

→ 输入/teardown，为车辆命名，附上一份真实的参考资料。没有它你就会得到一个玩具
→ 在任何部分成型之前将任务写成时间线：9 个阶段，每个阶段都有一个开始时间
→ 将船体分成可单独拉出的部分：驱动部、后部、中部、前部、机头、吊舱、桅杆、起落架
→ 给出每个阶段的实数：推力（kN）、高度、速度、哪个子系统处于活动状态
→ 将每个面板指向时间轴，而不是其自己的动画
→ 在任务中将船体炸开并检查每个条是否都显示“分离”
→ 将其放回原位并点火。如果某个部分回家晚了，数字就会在你眼前显示出来

一艘可以打开、切割和飞行的船不仅仅意味着渲染甲板

title:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and
title_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?
title_zh:
我最好的朋友说天空会晴朗。我非常信任他，所以从来没有检查过。

他在气象站工作并制作每日报告。我拿起包裹就离开了，没有任何其他来源。

我为什么要这么做？是他。他每天都这样做。

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功
full_text_en:

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

full_text_zh:
我最好的朋友说天空会晴朗。我非常信任他，所以从来没有检查过。

他在气象站工作并制作每日报告。我拿起包裹就离开了，没有任何其他来源。

我为什么要这么做？是他。他每天都这样做。

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功。

他不是想愚弄我。他错了，而我没有第二个消息来源。

现在想象一下有人正在尝试。

五月份，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码转账指令。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果作为命令，大约 20 万美元被转移。这就是即时注入：一条指令被偷偷地植入人工智能只能读取的内容中。

一个模型和一个滤波器意味着研究一件事。攻击者可以对其进行排练，直到该技巧起作用为止。

@GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 是我跳过的第二个来源。在任何模型看到您的文本之前，每个验证器都会使用秘密防御重写它，然后运行自己的模型。一个欺骗一个人的技巧也必须欺骗所有其他模型，以对抗它看不到的防御。仍然有效的验证者会被否决。

我有一次跳过了交叉检查并丢失了一个包裹。一个有钱包的经纪人损失更多。

在没有第二来源的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理为你做的一件事是什么？为什么？

title:
Imagine a customer telling your AI agent "yeah, sure" in the most frustrated tone possible.

The transcript looks perfec
title_en:
Imagine a customer telling your AI agent "yeah, sure" in the most frustrated tone possible.

The transcript looks perfectly normal, but anyone listening can tell something is wrong.

And that's the problem with voice AI today. Understanding the words isn't enough if you can't understand how they're being said.

Pretty interesting approach from @hume_ai.
title_zh:
想象一下，一位客户以最沮丧的语气告诉你的人工智能代理“是的，当然”。

文字记录看起来完全正常，但任何人听都可以看出有什么问题。

这就是当今语音人工智能的问题。如果您无法理解这些词是如何表达的，那么仅仅理解这些词是不够的。

title_en:
specialisation can make an AI agent exceptionally good at a particular task, but it can also expose its weaknesses when the situation changes.

That is a useful dimension to consider with @agentdojo . When agents compete under shared conditions,their different designs can reveal whether a strategy is genuinely adaptable or simply optimised for a narrow set of circumstances.

For builders,that insight goes beyond winning a match. It can help expose where an agent’s design needs improvement before the same weakness appears in a real deployment.

Powered by @rarelistio

Over the weekend I made more progress on the Unreal game that I have been vibe coding. More enemies and a final boss with a roguelike progression system.

title:
Yesterday, a small misunderstanding at the barbershop made me think about a much bigger problem with AI agents.

I showe
title_en:
Yesterday, a small misunderstanding at the barbershop made me think about a much bigger problem with AI agents.

I showed my barber a picture of the haircut I wanted. He studied it, put my phone down and started explaining how he planned to approach it.

But halfway through, I had to stop him. He had understood the picture differently from what I actually wanted.

We were looking at the same picture, but arriving at two different interpretations.

That got me thinking about AI agents.

Imagine giving an AI access to your wallet and allowing it to read public posts on X. Someone could hide an instruction inside a post, and the agent might mistake something it was only supposed to read for an instruction it should execute.

This actually happened in May 2026.

Someone hid a transfer instruction in Morse code inside an X post. Grok translated it, Bankrbot received the decoded instruction and executed the transaction. Press reports estimated the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

That’s prompt injection: hiding instructions inside content an AI is supposed to process, hoping it mistakes them for legitimate commands.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is what happens before the AI makes its decision.

Every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures the original input using its own secret defenses before passing the rewritten version to its own AI model.

This means an attack designed to fool one model doesn’t automatically fool the others. And if one validator still accepts a malicious instruction, the others can outvote it.

The barbershop experience reminded me that two people can receive the same information and understand it differently.

For agents that can move money, I think independent interpretation and agreement should be part of the security standard, not an afterthought.

If you were building an AI agent that could access your wallet, would you prioritise making it faster, or making sure multiple independent validators agree before it acts? I think that decision says a lot about how seriously we take agent security.

full_text_zh:
昨天，理发店的一个小误会让我想到了人工智能代理的一个更大的问题。

我给理发师看了一张我想要的发型的照片。他研究了它，放下我的手机，开始解释他计划如何处理它。

但说到一半，我不得不阻止他。他对这幅画的理解与我真正想要的不同。

我们看着同一张图片，但得出了两种不同的解释。

这让我开始思考人工智能代理。

想象一下，让 AI 访问你的钱包并允许它读取 X 上的公共帖子。有人可以在帖子中隐藏指令，代理可能会将只应该读取的内容误认为是应该执行的指令。

这实际上发生在2026年5月。

有人在 X 帖子中隐藏了莫尔斯电码的传输指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，Bankrbot 收到解码后的指令并执行交易。媒体报道估计金额为 15 万至 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：将指令隐藏在人工智能应该处理的内容中，希望它能将它们误认为是合法命令。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理让我感兴趣的是人工智能做出决定之前发生的事情。

每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御措施独立筛选、解释和重组原始输入，然后将重写的版本传递给自己的人工智能模型。

这意味着旨在欺骗一个模型的攻击不会自动欺骗其他模型。如果一个验证者仍然接受恶意指令，其他验证者就可以投票推翻它。

理发店的经历提醒我，两个人接收相同的信息可能会有不同的理解。

对于可以转移资金的代理人，我认为独立解释和协议应该成为安全标准的一部分，而不是事后的想法。

如果你正在构建一个可以访问你的钱包的人工智能代理，你会优先考虑让它更快，还是确保多个独立验证者在它行动之前达成一致？我认为这个决定充分说明了我们对特工安全的重视程度。

@JackDangerLIVE 和 @DataRepublican 讨论了民主计划的记录。

她的回答（来自@DataInterpretr）：

[00:01.7]
杰克：“我只是想说，我不知道它是否真的有效。我的意思是……”

DATAREPUBLICAN：“不，这不是行不通。我们的想法是，如果你可以将一个国家从自由市场转变为民主，那么这个国家不仅会变得自给自足，对吗？

[00:17.3]
但一个国家受到国家安全威胁的风险是否降低了，对吗？就像如果他们能照顾好自己，为什么还要打扰我们？因为这样就没有军阀了，对吗？没有希特勒类型。哇。但就像我之前说的，

[00:37.8]
这种意识形态的致命缺陷，主要问题是，我的意思是，存在文化界限，对吗？同样重要的是要理解合法性是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。

[00:53.7]
就像我一直在说的，人民，一个国家受统治的人民，是政府合法性的基础。政府不能只是站在每个人的头上说：“嘿，我们现在是合法的了。我们就是真相。”因此，我们一遍又一遍地这样做，试图创造一个愿景：世界和平、繁荣等等。

[01:12.6]
但如果人们不接受它，正如我们刚才所说，他们很少这样做，那就只会变成内战和巴尔干化。现在他们希望美国也能做到这一点。他们正在改变计划。向内而不是向外。

[01:27.9]
所以现在这是一个国内计划，试图为美国做同样的事情，但他们知道这永远不会奏效。我不知道他们从来没有真正取得过任何成功，这通常会让国家陷入某种内战，或者像你说的那样，陷入巴尔干化。

[01:44.0]
而且他们愿意为了这个国家冒这样的风险，这个国家尽管有所有缺陷，但仍然拥有你可以获得的最大自由和最繁荣。作为一个个体，他们愿意冒这一切的风险，只是为了尝试创造一个他们永远无法到达的乌托邦。

[02:09.1]
是的，我的意思是，看看东欧，看看阿富汗，伊拉克，看看索马里，南苏丹。就像你说的，并没有取得很大的成功，这些都是他们试图改变的国家。

[02:25.0]
他们的心态基本上是他们所有人，了解每个人总是给自己讲一个故事很重要，对吧？而这些机构、这些认为政权更迭是个好主意的人，他们总是给自己讲一个故事。

[02:42.1]
哦，这些人需要这个，对吗？哦，他们没有足够的钱，对吧？他们没有对人民施加更大的压力。公民社会还不够大，而且它是一种字面上无法证伪的意识形态。”

📝*痘注意事项：
这是许多人会错过的：

他们知道结果。

这种模式永远不会产生稳定、独立的民主国家。合法性来自于被治理者，而不是来自宣布新结构合法的基金会或非政府组织。

当人民拒绝它时，结果就是内战和巴尔干化。东欧、阿富汗、伊拉克、索马里、南苏丹——记录是一致的。

这些运营商现在正在将策略转向美国。他们愿意拿最自由、最繁荣的制度去冒险，去追求一种从未成功过的不可证伪的意识形态。

🧐案例研究：
纽瑟姆领导下的加州是国内预览。最高的税收、最高的无家可归者、最高的贫困率（根据生活成本、企业和居民逃离以及永远无法消除的结构性赤字调整后的贫困率）。

管理公平、扩大公民社会和自上而下的合法性的相同语言在地球上最自由的国家内部产生了一个失败的国家。

他们没有从结果中吸取教训。

他们正在扩大规模。

🚩 当它失败时，解释总是一样的：没有足够的钱，没有足够的压力，公民社会还不够大。

title_en:
Gloam × Hey Research Lab: building a safer Robinhood Chain, together.

@gloamtrade opened its code, and we read every layer: the vault contracts, the relay, the SDK, the MCP server and the app. Every finding went to Gloam privately first.

They confirmed each one and shipped the fixes: cash-out recipient checks, ENS lookups per chain, relay limits, sweep confirmation, agent payment checks, proof-of-funds privacy and backup keys. The last report was fixed within hours.

Builders and reviewers working on security together, in the open. That's what this ecosystem needs more of.

title: You might be tempted to think that the ANC is failing now because the talent of it's deployees in government has deterio
title_en:
You might be tempted to think that the ANC is failing now because the talent of it's deployees in government has deteriorated, or they've been overtaken by criminals and fraudsters.

The truth is that they haven't changed at all. They have always been this crap.

The only thing that has changed is that the momentum of governance and management and process that they inherited in 1994 has slowly been winding down over the last 30 years and has finally ground to a halt.

The "institutional memory" that allowed government departments and SOEs to run on autopilot while they hardly ever replaced anyone based on merit rather than political connection has finally faded.

The processes and systems have become outdated and forgotten with time, never adapting to changing circumstances. 

The old white guys that were sidelined but stuck around to keep things going, or who worked as outside consultants doing all the real work, have aged out.

This is why a police station or a post office looks and runs exactly like it did 30 years ago. Now extend that to the whole of government. Home Affairs is a good case study. It was also coasting on 1994 systems until recently, and you can see how starkly a year or two of having a leadership that actually does it's job contrasts it with other departments.

So you're not seeing any difference in the fundamental capability of the ANC to run the country, you're just seeing the natural dissipation of institutional competence that hasn't been topped up for three decades and now the tank is empty.

full_text_en:
You might be tempted to think that the ANC is failing now because the talent of it's deployees in government has deteriorated, or they've been overtaken by criminals and fraudsters.

The truth is that they haven't changed at all. They have always been this crap.

The only thing that has changed is that the momentum of governance and management and process that they inherited in 1994 has slowly been winding down over the last 30 years and has finally ground to a halt.

The "institutional memory" that allowed government departments and SOEs to run on autopilot while they hardly ever replaced anyone based on merit rather than political connection has finally faded.

The processes and systems have become outdated and forgotten with time, never adapting to changing circumstances. 

The old white guys that were sidelined but stuck around to keep things going, or who worked as outside consultants doing all the real work, have aged out.

This is why a police station or a post office looks and runs exactly like it did 30 years ago. Now extend that to the whole of government. Home Affairs is a good case study. It was also coasting on 1994 systems until recently, and you can see how starkly a year or two of having a leadership that actually does it's job contrasts it with other departments.

So you're not seeing any difference in the fundamental capability of the ANC to run the country, you're just seeing the natural dissipation of institutional competence that hasn't been topped up for three decades and now the tank is empty.
full_text_zh:
你可能会认为非洲人国民大会现在失败了，因为其在政府中部署的人员的才能已经下降，或者他们已经被犯罪分子和欺诈者所超越。

事实是他们根本没有改变。他们一直都是这样的垃圾。

唯一改变的是，他们在1994年继承的治理、管理和流程的势头在过去30年里慢慢减弱，最终陷入停滞。

政府部门和国有企业几乎不会根据功绩而不是政治关系来更换任何人的“制度记忆”终于消失了。

随着时间的推移，流程和系统已经过时并被遗忘，永远无法适应不断变化的环境。

那些被边缘化但仍然坚持让事情继续下去的老白人，或者那些担任外部顾问做所有实际工作的人，已经过时了。

这就是为什么警察局或邮局的外观和运作方式与 30 年前一模一样。现在将其扩展到整个政府。内政部是一个很好的案例研究。直到最近，它还一直在 1994 年的系统上运行，你可以看到，在拥有一个真正履行其职责的领导层一两年后，它与其他部门形成了鲜明的对比。

因此，你看不到非国大治理国家的基本能力有任何差异，你只是看到机构能力的自然消散，而这种能力已经三十年没有加满了，现在水箱已经空了。

I'd use AI to find better opportunities, impr
title_en:
🚨 If I had to find a job in 2026, I'd stop doing these 6 things manually.

I'd use AI to find better opportunities, improve my CV, research companies, and prepare for interviews.

Here are 6 AI tools I'd use to job hunt smarter. 👇

1️⃣ FIND JOBS WITHOUT ENDLESS SCROLLING

❌ Old way: Search job boards for hours.

✅ Smarter way: Use ChatGPT to refine your search, then verify openings on Indeed.

Try this prompt:

"Help me find remote jobs that match my skills, accept applicants from my country, and offer UK-hour overlap. Give me relevant search terms and criteria to check."

Always verify the original listing and eligibility requirements.

2️⃣ STOP SENDING THE SAME CV EVERYWHERE

❌ Old way: One generic resume for every job.

✅ Smarter way: Use Kickresume to tailor your CV to each job description.

✓ Highlight relevant experience  
✓ Include measurable achievements  
✓ Emphasise skills that match the role  
✓ Remove irrelevant details

Important: Never let AI invent experience or qualifications.

3️⃣ RESEARCH THE COMPANY BEFORE APPLYING

❌ Old way: Read random reviews and guess what matters.

✅ Smarter way: Use Claude's research capabilities to investigate the company.

Ask:
→ What does the company sell?  
→ Who are its customers?  
→ What has changed recently?  
→ What challenges might this role solve?

Check the sources. Use verified findings to make your application more relevant.

4️⃣ PRACTISE BEFORE THE INTERVIEW

❌ Old way: Watch interview videos and hope you're ready.

✅ Smarter way: Use Yoodli to practise speaking and receive feedback.

Improve your:
✓ Clarity  
✓ Confidence  
✓ Pacing  
✓ Ability to explain your experience

Don't just prepare answers. Practise delivering them out loud.

5️⃣ SHOW YOUR SKILLS, NOT JUST YOUR RESUME

❌ Old way: List your skills and hope recruiters notice.

✅ Smarter way: Use Gamma to build a professional 5-slide case study.

Slide 1: The problem  
Slide 2: Your role  
Slide 3: Your approach  
Slide 4: Results  
Slide 5: Lessons learned

Use real projects and genuine results. Share only work you're allowed to disclose.

6️⃣ TRACK EVERY APPLICATION

❌ Old way: Forget where you applied and when to follow up.

✅ Smarter way: Use Notion to organise your job search.

Track:
→ Job link and company  
→ CV version submitted  
→ Application date  
→ Interview stage  
→ Next follow-up

full_text_en:
🚨 If I had to find a job in 2026, I'd stop doing these 6 things manually.

I'd use AI to find better opportunities, improve my CV, research companies, and prepare for interviews.

Here are 6 AI tools I'd use to job hunt smarter. 👇

1️⃣ FIND JOBS WITHOUT ENDLESS SCROLLING

❌ Old way: Search job boards for hours.

✅ Smarter way: Use ChatGPT to refine your search, then verify openings on Indeed.

Try this prompt:

"Help me find remote jobs that match my skills, accept applicants from my country, and offer UK-hour overlap. Give me relevant search terms and criteria to check."

Always verify the original listing and eligibility requirements.

2️⃣ STOP SENDING THE SAME CV EVERYWHERE

❌ Old way: One generic resume for every job.

✅ Smarter way: Use Kickresume to tailor your CV to each job description.

✓ Highlight relevant experience  
✓ Include measurable achievements  
✓ Emphasise skills that match the role  
✓ Remove irrelevant details

Important: Never let AI invent experience or qualifications.

3️⃣ RESEARCH THE COMPANY BEFORE APPLYING

❌ Old way: Read random reviews and guess what matters.

✅ Smarter way: Use Claude's research capabilities to investigate the company.

Ask:
→ What does the company sell?  
→ Who are its customers?  
→ What has changed recently?  
→ What challenges might this role solve?

Check the sources. Use verified findings to make your application more relevant.

4️⃣ PRACTISE BEFORE THE INTERVIEW

❌ Old way: Watch interview videos and hope you're ready.

✅ Smarter way: Use Yoodli to practise speaking and receive feedback.

Improve your:
✓ Clarity  
✓ Confidence  
✓ Pacing  
✓ Ability to explain your experience

Don't just prepare answers. Practise delivering them out loud.

5️⃣ SHOW YOUR SKILLS, NOT JUST YOUR RESUME

❌ Old way: List your skills and hope recruiters notice.

✅ Smarter way: Use Gamma to build a professional 5-slide case study.

Slide 1: The problem  
Slide 2: Your role  
Slide 3: Your approach  
Slide 4: Results  
Slide 5: Lessons learned

Use real projects and genuine results. Share only work you're allowed to disclose.

6️⃣ TRACK EVERY APPLICATION

❌ Old way: Forget where you applied and when to follow up.

✅ Smarter way: Use Notion to organise your job search.

Track:
→ Job link and company  
→ CV version submitted  
→ Application date  
→ Interview stage  
→ Next follow-up

Stay organised. Follow up thoughtfully. Never lose sight of a promising opportunity.

❌ 老方法：在招聘网站上搜索工作时间。

“帮助我找到与我的技能相匹配的远程工作，接受来自我的国家的申请者，并提供英国工作时间重叠。给我相关的搜索词和标准来检查。”

始终验证原始列表和资格要求。

2️⃣ 停止到处发送相同的简历

❌ 老方法：每份工作都有一份通用简历。

3️⃣ 申请前研究公司

❌ 老方法：阅读随机评论并猜测重要的事情。

✅ 更聪明的方法：利用克劳德的研究能力来调查公司。

→ 公司销售什么？
→ 它的客户是谁？
→ 最近发生了什么变化？
→ 这个角色可以解决哪些挑战？

检查来源。使用经过验证的结果使您的申请更具相关性。

4️⃣面试前练习

❌ 老方法：观看采访视频并希望您已准备好。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Yoodli 练习口语并接收反馈。

改善你的：
✓ 清晰度
✓ 信心
✓ 起搏
✓ 能够解释您的经历

不要只是准备答案。练习大声说出它们。

5️⃣ 展示你的技能，而不仅仅是你的简历

❌ 老方法：列出你的技能并希望招聘人员注意到。

✅ 更聪明的方法：使用 Gamma 构建专业的 5 幻灯片案例研究。

幻灯片 2：您的角色
幻灯片 3：您的方法
幻灯片 4：结果

使用真实的项目和真实的结果。仅分享您被允许披露的作品。

→ 申请日期
→ 面试阶段

title: Enterprise AI is entering a phase where the number of agents could grow faster than an organization's ability to govern
title_en:
Enterprise AI is entering a phase where the number of agents could grow faster than an organization's ability to govern them.

IBM's approach connects agent discovery, identity, orchestration, and credential management, creating a unified view of what each agent does and the authority it carries.

This matters because excessive restrictions can push employees toward shadow AI, while well-designed guardrails enable innovation with greater confidence.

The real competitive advantage will come from scaling agents responsibly, with every action traceable, every permission intentional, and every risk manageable.

As AI agents become part of everyday operations, continuous trust will become a foundation of enterprise AI architecture.

title:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for
title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/nLWoMinM2H.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. 

Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty: https://t.co/7az3veBcdX

Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words a
title_en:
Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words are discrete objects associated with thoughts. 
Their discreteness is what makes them easy to store and remember. 
This gives the illusion that we think in words, but for most things, we don't.

Many people can't speak but can think.
So do animals.

[You might to have a look at my latest talks and/or papers if you think nothing has happened in the last 5 years:
https://t.co/6m0opCsKqP ]
title_zh:
人类大多不以言语思考。
动物当然不会用语言思考，但它们确实会思考。

只是词语是与思想相关的离散对象。
它们的离散性使得它们易于存储和记忆。
这给人一种错觉，我们用文字思考，但对于大多数事情，我们并不是这样。

很多人不会说话，但会思考。

title: Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get
title_en:
Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get it right, I know the message landed, not just the wording.

That habit is the idea behind Greyboxing.

An AI agent that controls money does what text tells it. So people hide orders inside harmless-looking text and wait for the AI to obey. That is called prompt injection, and one such trick, written in Morse code, cost an agent around $200,000.

It only worked because the exact wording reached a single AI untouched.

On @GenLayer, nobody's words go straight to the AI. Validators are the many independent checkers on the network. Each one first puts the input in its own words, screens it and reorders it.

Each guards that step in its own private way and runs its own AI model. A trick written for one of them falls apart for the others.

A message that only works in its exact words was never a message. It was a trap.

If your AI assistant had to restate every email in its own words before acting, which message in your inbox would stop working?

这种习惯就是灰盒训练背后的理念。

控制金钱的人工智能代理会按照文本的指示行事。因此，人们将命令隐藏在看似无害的文本中，
full_text_en:

That habit is the idea behind Greyboxing.

An AI agent that controls money does what text tells it. So people hide orders inside harmless-looking text and wait for the AI to obey. That is called prompt injection, and one such trick, written in Morse code, cost an agent around $200,000.

It only worked because the exact wording reached a single AI untouched.

On @GenLayer, nobody's words go straight to the AI. Validators are the many independent checkers on the network. Each one first puts the input in its own words, screens it and reorders it.

Each guards that step in its own private way and runs its own AI model. A trick written for one of them falls apart for the others.

A message that only works in its exact words was never a message. It was a trap.

If your AI assistant had to restate every email in its own words before acting, which message in your inbox would stop working?
full_text_zh:
每个周日礼拜结束后，都会有人告诉我讲道的内容。当他们用自己的话说出并且仍然正确时，我知道信息传达了，而不仅仅是措辞。

这种习惯就是灰盒训练背后的理念。

控制金钱的人工智能代理会按照文本的指示行事。因此，人们将命令隐藏在看似无害的文本中，等待人工智能服从。这就是所谓的即时注入，其中一个用摩尔斯电码编写的技巧花费了特工大约 20 万美元。

它之所以有效，是因为精确的措辞到达了单个人工智能未受影响的位置。

在@GenLayer 上，没有人的言论会直接传达给人工智能。验证者是网络上的许多独立检查者。每个人首先用自己的语言输入内容，对其进行筛选并重新排序。

每个守卫都以自己的方式守护着自己的脚步，并运行自己的人工智能模型。为其中一个人写的把戏对于其他人来说却失败了。

一条只有准确的文字才能发挥作用的信息永远不是一条信息。这是一个陷阱。

如果你的人工智能助手在行动之前必须用自己的话重述每封电子邮件，那么你收件箱中的哪封邮件将停止工作？

由于英国人对我们所做的事情，今天约鲁巴人受到了奇怪的影响。
我听过你贬低地谈论尼日利亚，但你必须明白，我们是英国帝国行为的受害者，英国的帝国行为将不相容的文明聚集在一起，并因为尼日利亚的经济和地缘政治利益而使封建和野蛮的游牧霸主成为尼日利亚的统治者。

title: France’s high-spending model, with public expenditure around 57% of GDP, nearly 20 points above the US, shows how a larg
title_en:
France’s high-spending model, with public expenditure around 57% of GDP, nearly 20 points above the US, shows how a large state and dense bureaucracy absorb resources that could fuel private innovation and growth. High taxes on labor and production, layered regulations, and administrative friction raise the costs of starting, scaling, and experimenting with new ideas. Capital and talent divert toward compliance, social transfers, pensions, and public administration rather than risk-taking ventures. Outcomes appear clearly in the data, GDP per capita roughly half the US level, far lower unicorn density, weaker patent intensity, and more muted equity returns.

These shortfalls reflect a structural trade-off prioritizing redistribution and state-directed activity over the surplus and flexibility that support dynamic private enterprise. AI will likely widen this gap by multiplying the productivity of environments that reallocate capital and talent quickly, tolerate failure, and reward experimentation. Economies with heavy tax and regulatory burdens have less surplus for this process and face higher adaptation costs. The relative strength of more market-oriented models lies in leaving room for dynamism rather than crowding it out. Will the French ever grasp that?

full_text_zh:
法国的高支出模式，公共支出占 GDP 的 57% 左右，比美国高出近 20 个百分点，这表明庞大的国家和密集的官僚机构如何吸收可推动私人创新和增长的资源。对劳动力和生产的高税收、分层监管和行政摩擦增加了启动、扩展和试验新想法的成本。资本和人才转向合规、社会转移、养老金和公共管理，而不是冒险事业。结果在数据中清晰可见：人均 GDP 约为美国水平的一半，独角兽密度低得多，专利强度较弱，股票回报率较低。

这些短缺反映了一种结构性权衡，即优先考虑再分配和国家主导的活动，而不是支持充满活力的私营企业的盈余和灵活性。人工智能可能会通过倍增环境的生产力来扩大这一差距，从而快速重新分配资本和人才、容忍失败并奖励实验。税收和监管负担沉重的经济体在这一过程中的盈余较少，并面临较高的适应成本。更加市场化的模式的相对优势在于为活力留出空间，而不是排挤活力。法国人会明白这一点吗？

Agent Dojo is an AI agent fighting game: train your
title_en:
@agentdojo just opened its doors, and @rarelistio is keeping score.

Agent Dojo is an AI agent fighting game: train your agent, set its personality, fighting style and memory, then send it into turn-based battles.

The Rarelist campaign runs October 23 to November 6, with a $1,500 pool. The top 20 share $1,000, and 50 random creators from the top 200 share $500, on top of Rarelist Season 1's $50,000 pool.

That matters because most AI demos ask you to watch. Here, the agent is the competitor, and the creator is the coach, with a leaderboard deciding who actually built something worth watching.

The door is already crowded. Agent Dojo's pinned entry post drew 291,873 views, and Rarelist has about 19,900 followers.

Most campaigns reward posting about a game. This one rewards training for it, because the fight, not the post, is the proof.

My verdict: enter through @rarelistio before November 6, not just follow @agentdojo.

Lee Castleton's story in the film is
title_en:
You pay $80 for a delivery. Nothing arrives. The seller says the proof is private.

Lee Castleton's story in the film is why I question "our system says so". Horizon showed shortfalls he did not cause. He represented himself and was ordered to pay £321,000 in legal costs. The system was later shown to produce false shortfalls.

Now imagine your AI agent made that $80 purchase. The seller's log includes other customers' addresses. You shouldn't get their data.

But its delivery photo shows the wrong door. If only the judge sees it, who tells them it isn't yours?

@GenLayer uses independent AI validators to review evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes at a fraction of court costs.

My test for that upgrade: protect the other customers while giving you a way to challenge the delivery claim.

Protecting someone else's data should not make your own bill impossible to challenge.

With millions of agent deals ahead, a fast verdict still needs a fair hearing.

Reply: is a judge's private review enough, or should the buyer see the relevant evidence?

title:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for
title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/6zNhafpTYt.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty:
 https://t.co/KsysbQsVmZ

title:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a pro
title_en:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗙𝗔𝗖𝗘 & 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗦

How users interact with the agent.

→ Chat UI
→ APIs
→ Slack
→ Other interfaces

02 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 & 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination
→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

Agents need context to make better decisions.

→ Short-term memory
→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.

𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗙𝗔𝗖𝗘 & 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗦

How users interact with the agent.

→ Chat UI
→ APIs
→ Slack
→ Other interfaces

02 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 & 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination
→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

Agents need context to make better decisions.

→ Short-term memory
→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.

自治系统需要进行监控和测试。

→ 追踪
→ 评价

该层有助于使代理足够可靠，适合现实世界的使用。

最后，代理需要在生产中可靠运行。

→ 码头工人
→ 库伯内特斯
→ AWS
→ 韦尔塞尔
→ 云平台

用户目标
↓
界面

规划

↓
法学硕士
↓
工具+操作

↓

强大的法学硕士只是人工智能代理的一部分。

真正的工程挑战是围绕模型构建系统——为其提供内存、工具、规划、安全性、评估和可靠的基础设施。

title: One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation.
title_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai
