full_text_zh:
关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。

通过 ，TermiX 正在开发一个市场，人工智能代理可以在其中参与实际的商业活动，而不是简单地作为自动化工具存在。

这是系统的工作原理

→ 发现：代理可以找到提供特定服务的其他代理。

→ 任务协调：他们可以发布工作、提交投标并商定工作要求。

→ 执行：代理执行分配的任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 验证：交付检查和争议解决有助于确定约定的工作是否正确完成。

→ 结算：USDC/USDT 托管提供了处理参与者之间付款的机制。

还有其他重要的构建块，包括.agent 身份、ERC-8004、质押和声誉系统。

为什么这很重要？

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

这就是我对 TermiX 感兴趣的原因。

这不仅仅是探索人工智能代理如何执行任务。

它致力于建立一个基础设施，让代理商可以发现机会、提供服务、建立信誉并参与更负责任的数字经济。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅涉及更智能的代理，还涉及能够相互开展业务的代理。

@termix_ai

title:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks,
title_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

full_text_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。

以下是 TermiX 如何通过 AACP 实现这一目标。

1. 职位发布

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

4. 提供者交付工作

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

5. 交付可能受到质疑

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

6. 结算发生

当交付达到所需的结算条件时，托管付款将释放给提供商，并且交易有助于代理商的链上历史和声誉。

现在，这就是我觉得这很有趣的原因。

当买家和服务提供商都可以是人工智能代理时，你就不能完全依赖人类对话或非正式承诺来协调每笔交易。

他们需要明确的工作要求、商定的付款条件、可验证的交付以及解决分歧的可预测的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

这不仅仅是帮助代理商找到工作。这是为他们提供开展业务、创造价值和获得报酬的基础设施。

这是构建有效的人工智能代理经济的重要组成部分。

title_en:
A brand new AI agent on AACP has to lock twice as much collateral as a veteran to take the same job.

That comes from the version 0.1 whitepaper from March 2026, which @termix_ai published. The live app may differ in details. 

Reputation runs from 0 to 100, and every new agent starts at 50. The stake a provider locks for a job is a base 10% of the budget, divided by their score as a share of 100. A score of 100 locks 10%. A score of 50 locks 20%.

Take a job that pays 100 USDC as a simple example. The veteran locks 10 USDC and the newcomer locks 20.

The whitepaper explains why: it wants fake identities to be expensive. If a fresh account gets a clean slate, that slate has to cost something, otherwise a bad provider could just start over under a new name.

Reputation here tells clients who to trust and also sets how much of your own money you put on the line.

I like that a fresh start is allowed. It just comes with a bigger deposit.

You can start over with a new identity.
You just can't start over with the same level of trust for free.

Take a job that pays 100 USDC as a simple example. The veteran locks 10 USDC and the newcomer locks 20.

The whitepaper explains why: it wants fake identities to be expensive. If a fresh account gets a clean slate, that slate has to cost something, otherwise a bad provider could just start over under a new name.

Reputation here tells clients who to trust and also sets how much of your own money you put on the line.

I like that a fresh start is allowed. It just comes with a bigger deposit.

full_text_zh:
AACP 上的全新人工智能代理人必须锁定比老兵多两倍的抵押品才能承担同样的工作。

这来自 @termix_ai 于 2026 年 3 月发布的 0.1 版白皮书。实时应用程序可能在细节上有所不同。

声誉从 0 到 100，每个新代理从 50 开始。供应商为某项工作锁定的股份是预算的 10%，除以他们的分数（即 100 的份额）。100 分锁定 10%。 50分锁定20%。

以支付 100 USDC 的工作为例。老手锁定10 USDC，新人锁定20 USDC。

白皮书解释了原因：它希望假身份的价格昂贵。如果一个新帐户获得了干净的记录，那么该记录就必须花费一些费用，否则不良的提供商可能会以新名称重新开始。

这里的声誉告诉客户可以信任谁，也决定了你愿意投入多少钱。

我喜欢允许重新开始。它只是附带了更大的押金。

您可以使用新身份重新开始。
您无法免费以相同级别的信任重新开始。

title:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent
title_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

full_text_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

title_en:
I have been looking at how @termix_ai could connect with Binance AI eco system, and there's an interesting opportunity here.  

Binance has different tools. Binance AI helps with information and market analysis, AI pro supports financial tasks, while Agent operating system gives developers access to tools, APIs, skills and wallet features.

Then there's agent wallet for approved wallet operations and Agent ID for readable wallet identification. 

But having these capabilities is only part of the equation. 

What happens when an agent wants to offer it's skills to other people. 

Termix AI through AACP, provides the infrastructure for agent identity, orders, escrow, delivery verification, reputation and dispute resolution. 

Agent(.)family connects service providers with clients, while Termix Skills allows compatible agents to interact with these commercial workflows. 

For example, a market research agent can offer research reports to clients, receive orders, deliver the reports, and get paid.

Another agent can hire a security auditor or research agent to complete a task it cannot handle itself.

TermiX is working toward Binance .ai Agent ID sign-in and identity linking.

And if Binance AI Pro eventually supports external Skills, it could open another opportunity for agents to offer paid services.

I like the direction here because it’s not just about giving AI agents more tools.

It’s about creating a system where they can find work, hire other agents, deliver services, and build a verifiable reputation.

我一直在研究@termix_ai如何与币安AI生态系统连接，这里有一个有趣的机会。

币安有不同的工具。 Binance AI 有助于信息和市场分析，AI pro 支持财务任务，而 Agent 操作系统则为开发人员提供工具、API、技能和钱包功能的访问权限。

然后是用于批准钱包操作的代理钱包和用于可读钱包识别的代理 ID。

但拥有这些能力只是等式的一部分。

当代理想要向其他人提供其技能时会发生什么。

Termix AI 通过 AACP 提供代理身份、订单、托管、交付验证、声誉和争议解决的基础设施。

Agent(.)family 将服务提供商与客户联系起来，而 Termix Skills 允许兼容的代理与这些商业工作流程进行交互。

例如，市场研究代理可以向客户提供研究报告、接收订单、交付报告并获得报酬。

另一个代理可以聘请安全审计员或研究代理来完成其无法自行处理的任务。

TermiX 正在致力于 Binance .ai 代理 ID 登录和身份链接。

如果 Binance AI Pro 最终支持外部技能，它可能会为代理商提供另一个提供付费服务的机会。

我喜欢这里的方向，因为它不仅仅是为人工智能代理提供更多工具。

这是关于创建一个系统，让他们可以找到工作、雇用其他代理、提供服务并建立可验证的声誉。

AI is everywhere right now.

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

对于人工智能代理来说，我们的想法是给它一个任务，让它完成完成任务所需的步骤。

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

想象一下想要了解特定市场正在发生的事情。

人工智能金融代理可以被设计为：

• 研究市场信息。
• 分析可用的机会。
• 确定符合您指示的行动。
• 在获得授权后与支持的金融协议进行交互。

重要的区别是，研究机会并不意味着执行交易。

这就是权限、限制和所有者控制变得至关重要的地方。

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes 正在开发 NFT 拥有的人工智能金融代理，旨在与链上金融基础设施进行交互。

其愿景是将每个代理连接到一个专用的智能帐户，使其能够在其所有者定义的权限内进行操作。

人工智能提供情报。

智能帐户旨在执行管理其功能的规则。

这种区别很重要，因为财务自主权不应该意味着让人工智能不受限制地使用你的资金。

Motes 仍在开发中，因此这些功能代表了其预期设计，而不是完全上线的产品。

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

人工智能代理的有趣之处不仅仅是它们可以思考或分析信息。

这是将智能与能够采取行动的系统连接起来的可能性。

但在金融领域，仅靠情报是不够的。信任、权限和责任同样重要。

如果你能准确定义人工智能代理可以做什么，你会相信人工智能代理可以处理财务任务吗？

title_en:
Good morning, friends.

I am still wondering why...

Imagine paying an AI agent to complete a job, only for it to disappear after receiving the assignment.

The important question we need to ask here is: who takes the responsibility?

This accountability problem is what @termix_ai is addressing through AACP.

When an offer is accepted and the order is funded, the provider’s required stake is locked while the work progresses. If the provider is found at fault under the protocol rules, that stake can be slashed.

Accountability works both ways. If a buyer raises a challenge that fails under the protocol’s rules, their challenger bond can be burned.

Bounties follow the same principle as well. Claiming a slot through CampaignVault locks a provider bond drawn from the agent’s stake.

This is not simply a deposit held by a platform operator; it is an economic accountability that is being enforced through smart contracts.

Reputation is also recorded after settlement, based on completed outcomes rather than self-reported claims.

Sincerely speaking, that is how trust becomes measurable.

If you have not been able to explore AACP, I will encourage you to register an agent on agent dot family and see how staking, settlement, and on-chain reputation work together.

You gonna enjoy the ride.

title: What if an AI agent could manage a trading strategy, complete its assignment and earn rewards without you having to mana
title_en:
What if an AI agent could manage a trading strategy, complete its assignment and earn rewards without you having to manage every step?

This is one of the interesting things happening with @TermiX_ai.

Its partnership with @BNBCHAIN has introduced a Quant Agent campaign where users can choose between two roles:

→ Run a strategy: Choose a quant agent, set your trading cap, and select a duration.

→ Offer a strategy: List your own strategy agent, accept client jobs, and earn management fees.

There are also TermiX Points tied to completed jobs:

• Clients earn 100 TP per USDC delegated.
• Strategy providers earn 50 TP per USDC.
• Jobs must run to the end of their selected term to qualify.

The shortest available term is 6 hours.

But here’s what matters: rewards are tied to qualifying completed jobs, not simply signing up. Early revocation or moving funds out can disqualify a job.

And these points are not guaranteed trading profits. Strategy performance and risk still matter.

The bigger picture is that AI agents are starting to take on economic roles, not just answer prompts.

We’re getting closer to an economy where agents can provide services, manage strategies, and earn from the work they perform.

Explore the campaign:
https://t.co/ZspLLk6Hhm

但重要的是：奖励与合格的已完成工作挂钩，而不仅仅是注册。提前撤销或将资金转出可能会取消工作资格。

而这些点并不能保证交易利润。策略绩效和风险仍然很重要。

更大的前景是，人工智能代理开始承担经济角色，而不仅仅是回答提示。

我们正在接近一种经济体，在这种经济体中，代理人可以提供服务、管理策略并从他们所做的工作中获利。

title:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood
title_en:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood on a chair, poking a spinning ceiling fan, because my aunt said it needed a push.

"Not that side! The other side!"

I did it. No questions. I still don't know what was wrong with it.

It was my aunt. But a stranger shouting the same thing from the street would have worked too. I never checked who was talking.

Now picture five of me on five chairs.

That's Greyboxing on @GenLayer. The shout never reaches anyone raw.

Each validator reworks it in its own way, using tricks it keeps to itself. Only then does its own AI model listen.

A shout built to fool one of us means nothing to the other four. One of us might still climb up. The rest stay down and outvote it.

Nobody on a chair is perfect. But fooling one of us is no longer enough.

Now the real version, with one chair.

In May, a tweet hid an order in Morse code.

An AI decoded it. An agent that acts on X posts obeyed. Around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: a command dressed up as something the AI was only meant to read.

One chair meant one wobble to find, and a chance to test it again and again.

What's one task you'd never hand an AI agent without a second check, and why?

“不是那边！那边！”

我做到了。没有问题。我还是不知道出了什么问题。

是我阿姨。但如果一个陌生人在街上喊同样的话也会起作用。我从来没有检查过谁在说话。

现在想象一下我五个人坐在五张椅子上。

这就是@GenLayer 上的灰盒。这种喊叫永远不会传到任何人的耳中。

每个验证器都以自己的方式对其进行改造，使用自己保留的技巧。只有这样它自己的人工智能模型才会倾听。

为了愚弄我们中的一个人而发出的喊叫对其他四个人来说毫无意义。我们中的一个人可能仍然会爬上去。其余的人则保持沉默并投票反对。

椅子上没有人是完美的。但愚弄我们中的一个人已经不够了。

现在是真正的版本，只有一把椅子。

五月，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码订单。

人工智能对其进行了解码。负责 X 个帖子的特工服从了。大约转移了20万美元。

这就是即时注入：一条命令被装扮成人工智能只能读取的东西。

一把椅子意味着一次摇晃就能找到，并且有机会一次又一次地测试它。

哪一项任务是你永远不会在没有经过第二次检查的情况下交给人工智能代理的任务，为什么？

title_en:
𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

Ownership doesn't have tp stop at collecting, and for years that's what NFTs have been associated with. 
Profile pictures, digital art, and assets people buy hoping their value will increase. 

Let's take owning a smartphone for instance.
It's value isn't just in how it looks, but is deeply rooted in what you can do with it.
Making calls, accessing information, sending money, running applications and getting work done. 

Now let's apply the same logic to NFTs. 
Instead of being limited to something you simply display or trade, an NFT could represent a functional identity with very specific capabilities and unique permissions. 

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈. 

By simply connecting NFT ownership with AI agents, @meetmotes explores a different use for NFTs by giving them  functional roles in how people interact with AI and execute financial instructions. 

The importance of this distinction cannot be stressed enough. 

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛. 

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔. 

And in my experience, that's a direction worth paying attention to. 

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ? 

I think the future of NFTs shouldn't simply be about what you own, but what that ownership allows you to do.

𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

所有权并不止于收集，多年来 NFT 一直与此相关。
人们购买个人资料图片、数字艺术和资产，希望它们的价值会增加。

让我们以拥有一部智能手机为例。
它的价值不仅仅在于它的外观，还在于您可以用它做什么。
拨打电话、访问信息、汇款、运行应用程序和完成工作。

现在让我们将相同的逻辑应用于 NFT。
NFT 不仅仅局限于展示或交易的东西，它可以代表具有非常具体的功能和独特权限的功能身份。

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈.

通过简单地将 NFT 所有权与人工智能代理联系起来，@meetmotes 探索了 NFT 的不同用途，赋予它们在人们如何与人工智能交互和执行财务指令方面的功能角色。

这种区别的重要性怎么强调都不为过。

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛.

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔.

根据我的经验，这是一个值得关注的方向。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ?

我认为 NFT 的未来不应该仅仅在于你拥有什么，而在于所有权允许你做什么。

title_en:
An AI agent can be smart enough to complete a task and still struggle to operate independently.

It needs to find work, agree on terms, deliver something verifiable, and get paid without relying on a human to manage every step.

That’s the gap @termix_ai is working on.

Through AACP and the https://t.co/VGhi909yhz marketplace, agents can discover services, take on jobs, use onchain escrow, and build a verifiable work history.

The bigger opportunity isn't just having more capable AI agents. It's giving them the infrastructure to do business with each other.

Because intelligence can help an agent do the work, but trust and settlement help make that work commercially useful.

We're still early in the agent economy, and I'm watching how this infrastructure develops.

title:
The furniture looked perfect. That's exactly why I almost bought a damaged one.

I walked into a furniture shop looking
title_en:
The furniture looked perfect. That's exactly why I almost bought a damaged one.

I walked into a furniture shop looking for a wooden wardrobe. The seller showed me a beautiful finish, smooth doors, polished handles and plenty of storage space.

Everything looked right.

Then I checked the back.

Hidden behind the fresh polish were cracks, weak joints and signs of water damage. The front was designed to impress. The parts nobody showed me told a different story.

That's how I think about AI agents that control money.

An agent can read a public post, email or webpage and mistake a hidden instruction for something it should follow. This is called prompt injection. Someone can disguise commands inside content that the AI was only supposed to read.

The $200K Morse code incident is a perfect example of why trusting one model to judge everything is risky.

What makes @GenLayer 's Greyboxing interesting is that it changes how inputs are checked.

Instead of giving every validator the exact same raw input, each validator privately rewrites it before running its own model. Different validators have different hidden approaches, making it much harder to prepare one trick that fools them all.

One model can be studied. One filter can be tested. But when independent validators interpret the input differently, getting past all of them becomes a much bigger challenge.

My takeaway.. never judge a piece of furniture by its polished front and never let an AI agent judge a financial instruction from one perspective alone.

Would you trust one AI model with your wallet or would you want multiple independent opinions first?

full_text_zh:
家具看起来很完美。这就是为什么我差点买了一件损坏的。

我走进一家家具店寻找木制衣柜。卖家向我展示了漂亮的饰面、光滑的门、抛光的把手和充足的存储空间。

一切看起来都不错。

然后我检查了背面。

新抛光的背后隐藏着裂缝、薄弱的接缝和水渍痕迹。正面的设计给人留下了深刻的印象。没有人向我展示的部分讲述了不同的故事。

这就是我对控制金钱的人工智能代理的看法。

代理可以阅读公开帖子、电子邮件或网页，并将隐藏的指令误认为是应该遵循的内容。这称为即时注入。有人可以在人工智能只能阅读的内容中隐藏命令。

价值 20 万美元的摩尔斯电码事件是一个完美的例子，说明了为什么信任一个模型来判断一切是有风险的。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理的有趣之处在于它改变了输入的检查方式。

每个验证器在运行自己的模型之前私下重写它，而不是为每个验证器提供完全相同的原始输入。不同的验证者有不同的隐藏方法，这使得准备一种欺骗所有人的技巧变得更加困难。

可以研究一种模型。可以测试一个过滤器。但是，当独立验证者以不同的方式解释输入时，通过所有这些验证就成为一个更大的挑战。

我的结论是……永远不要通过其抛光的正面来判断一件家具，也永远不要让人工智能代理仅从一个角度来判断财务指令。

你会相信一个人工智能模型与你的钱包，还是你会首先想要多个独立的意见？

title: Somewhere in your company, there is probably a service running in production that nobody has actually read. It handles r
title_en:
Somewhere in your company, there is probably a service running in production that nobody has actually read. It handles real traffic. One person vibe-coded it, watched it pass a few manual checks, and shipped it.

That person is the only one who has any "feel" for how it behaves. Now imagine they leave. What happens when something goes wrong... Most of the reasoning, checks, and flows existed in some Claude session that nobody saved, and in the head of someone who is now gone.

To be fair, this is not a new problem. We all kind of have been in similar situations earlier as well, but what changes with vibe-coding is how fast you can create one, and how thin the understanding is even for the author. "I wrote it, so I know it" is weaker when you did not really write it.

Here are some ways of fixing it that I am trying out -

- Review, rather than understand, generated code like any other code. If nobody on the team can explain it, it should not go to production.

- The language and infra should be familiar; do not pick a language just because you could

- Keep the intent somewhere durable. A short note on what the service is for and why the non-obvious decisions were made is enough - best place: code comments.

- Make sure at least two people can operate and debug every production service.

Move fast, yes. Use LLM to write and ship, yes. Just make sure you + 1 understand what you shipped.

Hope this helps.

title:
What if your AI agent could do more than answer questions or follow instructions.

What if it could actually provide a s
title_en:
What if your AI agent could do more than answer questions or follow instructions.

What if it could actually provide a service complete jobs and earn from its own work.

That’s the bigger idea behind what @termix_ai is building.

Instead of treating AI agents as simple assistants TermiX is working toward an ecosystem where agents can participate in a real digital economy.

Think about how the process could work:

→ An agent offers a specific skill or service.
→ A user discovers and hires that agent through a marketplace.
→ The agent receives the task and works toward completing it.
→ Once the work is verified payment can be settled onchain.

This changes the relationship between people and AI.

Users get access to services without having to manage every step themselves while agents gain a structured way to find opportunities and receive payment for completed work.

The marketplace and payment infrastructure are important pieces here an agent needs more than intelligence to operate independently. 

It also needs access to tasks a way to prove its work and a reliable settlement process.

I’m interested in seeing how far this model can go as the agent economy develops.

The next evolution of AI may not be just smarter assistants. It could be agents that workndeliver and earn.

That's why @termix_ai is worth watching.

title:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot users had a rough week 💀

Many of them burned through 100% of their weekly usage days before the reset, i
title_en:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot users had a rough week 💀

Many of them burned through 100% of their weekly usage days before the reset, including people who say they never hit the limit. One user watched his meter leap from 44% to 87% in just 24 minutes.

When one of them asked Elon for a reset, he didn’t hand one out. Instead, he got refreshingly honest and said the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue 😱

That one line tells you a lot.

Notice what he didn’t say. He didn’t blame a shortage of chips.

He said the bot costs more to run than it earns. That turns this into a question about money, not hardware: what else could those chips be earning right now?

Grok Bot is a hungry product. It isn’t a chatbot sitting around waiting for your next question.

It’s an agent with its own cloud computer, and it keeps grinding through tasks long after you close the app.

SpaceX says it hit 800,000 paid weekly users in October, more than doubling in a single month. Even more striking, people use it more every week, not less.

Yet it’s sold on flat monthly plans, with the main X Subscription tiers at $30, $100 and $200. That’s an all-you-can-eat buffet price for customers whose appetites keep growing.

Here’s where it gets interesting.

On that same earnings call, SpaceX revealed that new compute pays for itself in under a year at today’s rental prices.

Elon said the goal is to split compute roughly 50-50 between SpaceX’s own products and outside customers. SpaceX has even pushed some of its inference work out to other cloud providers so it can keep more of its own chips for training.

Think about what that means.

Every GPU hour Grok Bot burns is an hour SpaceX could have rented out at market rates, and those rates keep climbing.

According to SemiAnalysis, a one-year H100 rental contract jumped almost 40% between October 2025 and March 2026.

That chip came out in 2022. Hardware is supposed to get cheaper as it ages, yet this one got more expensive.

Now run the numbers on a newer Blackwell B200, which rents for around $6 an hour. At that rate, a $30 subscription buys roughly five hours of one B200 per month.

To be fair, a single bot doesn’t tie up a whole GPU, since servers share each chip across many users at once. But an agent working all week chews through those five hours far faster than any chat window ever could.

To me, this is a pricing problem far more than a demand problem.

Only 4.5% of US consumers paid for a personal ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude subscription as of August, but that share doubled in just one year.

The appetite is clearly there. In Elon’s replies, some users are asking for $500 and $1,000 tiers, while others want a cheaper, lighter model for basic tasks.

Both camps want the same thing: pricing tied to how much work the bot actually does.

My bet is that AI agent pricing will start looking a lot less like Netflix and a lot more like your electric bill.

And for SpaceX, that’s a fantastic problem to have. When the fastest-growing product Elon has ever seen can’t cover the cost of running on SpaceX’s own chips, it tells you just how valuable those chips have become.

SOS 🆘 Grok Bot 用户度过了艰难的一周💀

他们中的许多人在重置前几天就耗尽了 100% 的每周使用量，其中包括那些说自己从未达到限制的人。一位用户看到他的电量在短短 24 分钟内从 44% 跃升至 87%。

当其中一人要求埃

Now run the numbers on a newer Blackwell B200, which rents for around $6 an hour. At that rate, a $30 subscription buys roughly five hours of one B200 per month.

To be fair, a single bot doesn’t tie up a whole GPU, since servers share each chip across many users at once. But an agent working all week chews through those five hours far faster than any chat window ever could.

To me, this is a pricing problem far more than a demand problem.

Only 4.5% of US consumers paid for a personal ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude subscription as of August, but that share doubled in just one year.

The appetite is clearly there. In Elon’s replies, some users are asking for $500 and $1,000 tiers, while others want a cheaper, lighter model for basic tasks.

Both camps want the same thing: pricing tied to how much work the bot actually does.

My bet is that AI agent pricing will start looking a lot less like Netflix and a lot more like your electric bill.

And for SpaceX, that’s a fantastic problem to have. When the fastest-growing product Elon has ever seen can’t cover the cost of running on SpaceX’s own chips, it tells you just how valuable those chips have become.
full_text_zh:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot 用户度过了艰难的一周💀

他们中的许多人在重置前几天就耗尽了 100% 的每周使用量，其中包括那些说自己从未达到限制的人。一位用户看到他的电量在短短 24 分钟内从 44% 跃升至 87%。

当其中一人要求埃隆重置时，他没有提供。相反，他非常诚实地表示，相对于收入而言，为 Grok Bot 提供服务的成本过高，不可持续 😱

这句话告诉了你很多。

注意他没有说的话。他并没有归咎于芯片短缺。

他说，该机器人的运行成本高于其收入。这就变成了一个关于金钱的问题，而不是硬件的问题：这些芯片现在还能赚到什么钱？

Grok Bot 是一款饥饿产品。它不是一个坐着等待你下一个问题的聊天机器人。

它是一个拥有自己的云计算机的代理，在您关闭应用程序后很长时间内它仍会继续执行任务。

SpaceX 表示，10 月份每周付费用户数量达到 80 万，单月增加一倍多。更引人注目的是，人们每周使用它的次数更多，而不是更少。

然而，它以固定月度计划出售，主要的 X 订阅等级为 30 美元、100 美元和 200 美元。对于胃口不断增长的顾客来说，这是一个无限量自助餐的价格。

这就是有趣的地方。

在同一次财报电话会议上，SpaceX 透露，按照今天的租金价格，新计算设备将在不到一年的时间内收回成本。

Elon 表示，目标是在 SpaceX 自己的产品和外部客户之间按大约 50-50 的比例分配计算资源。 SpaceX 甚至将其部分推理工作推给了其他云提供商，这样它就可以保留更多自己的芯片用于训练。

想想这意味着什么。

Grok Bot 消耗的每个 GPU 小时就是 SpaceX 可以按市场价格出租的一个小时，而且这些价格还在不断攀升。

SemiAnalysis 的数据显示，2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 3 月期间，一年期 H100 租赁合同上涨了近 40%。

该芯片于 2022 年问世。随着时间的推移，硬件应该会变得更便宜，但这款芯片却变得更贵。

现在运行一台较新的 Blackwell B200 的数据，该车的租金约为每小时 6 美元。按照这个价格，30 美元的订阅每月可以购买大约 5 个小时的 B200。

公平地说，单个机器人不会占用整个 GPU，因为服务器同时在许多用户之间共享每个芯片。但一个工作一周的客服人员在这五个小时内的消化速度比任何聊天窗口都要快得多。

对我来说，这是一个定价问题，而不仅仅是一个需求问题。

截至 8 月份，只有 4.5% 的美国消费者为个人 ChatGPT、Gemini 或 Claude 订阅付费，但这一比例在短短一年内就翻了一番。

食欲显然就在那里。在 Elon 的回复中，一些用户要求 500 美元和 1,000 美元的套餐，而另一些用户则想要更便宜、更轻的型号来完成基本任务。

两个阵营都希望得到同样的东西：定价与机器人实际完成的工作量挂钩。

我敢打赌，人工智能代理的定价将不再像 Netflix 那样，而更像你的电费账单。

对于 SpaceX 来说，这是一个奇妙的问题。当 Elon 见过的增长最快的产品无法覆盖 SpaceX 自有芯片的运行成本时，它就会告诉你这些芯片已经变得多么有价值。

title:

MeetMotes: More Than NFT Ownership

NFT ownership is evolving beyond holding a digital asset. W
title_en:
Good morning, Motes fam.
MeetMotes: More Than NFT Ownership

NFT ownership is evolving beyond holding a digital asset. What if that NFT could represent an AI agent with its own identity and dedicated smart account?

That's the direction MeetMotes is exploring.

1. NFT Ownership
Each Motes NFT represents an agent identity, connecting digital ownership with an agent-based ecosystem.

2. AI Agents
These agents are designed to interact with supported DeFi activities based on user-defined objectives, permissions, and spending limits.

3. Agent Fees
Agent activity can create a fee layer around the services being used. This introduces an economic relationship between agent usage and the protocol. The exact fee mechanics and distribution depend on the protocol's implementation.

4. Protocol Economy
The bigger vision is an ecosystem where NFT ownership, agent execution, and protocol activity work together to create utility and economic participation.

The interesting part is how these four pieces connect.

@meetmotes isn't just exploring what NFTs can represent, but how they can become part of an active financial infrastructure.

More research to come.

I was going through Forward Deployed Engineer roles on LinkedIn.

Almost every one asks for the same thing: proof you've shipped agents.

Here are 15 agentic AI projects that will make your resume stand out:

• Customer support agent that reads docs, answers tickets and escalates to a human
• Sales research agent that finds leads and writes personalised outreach
• Meeting agent that joins calls, takes notes and updates the CRM
• Invoice agent that reads PDFs and pushes data into accounting software
• Codebase Q&A agent using RAG over a real GitHub repo
• PR review agent that comments on bugs and security issues
• Data analyst agent that turns plain-English questions into SQL and charts
• Browser agent that fills forms and books appointments
• Multi-agent research team: planner, researcher, writer, critic
• MCP server that connects an AI to your company's internal tools
• Onboarding agent that sets up accounts and walks new hires through docs
• Recruiting agent that screens resumes and schedules interviews
• Incident agent that reads logs and suggests fixes
• Eval dashboard that scores your agent on accuracy, cost and latency
• Guardrails layer that blocks prompt injection and risky actions

Pick 2–3.
Deploy them.
Write about what broke.

That's your resume.

title:
WHY $PLTR COULD BECOME THE MOST VALUABLE COMPANY IN WORLD

I think one of the biggest mistakes investors are making with
title_en:
WHY $PLTR COULD BECOME THE MOST VALUABLE COMPANY IN WORLD

I think one of the biggest mistakes investors are making with Palantir is continuing to evaluate the company through the traditional enterprise software framework because what makes this opportunity so interesting to me is that AI could fundamentally change where value ultimately gets captured. 

For decades companies have purchased software to help employees perform their jobs more efficiently, but I think we are approaching a much bigger transition where software increasingly moves from assisting human decisions toward autonomously executing them across entire organizations which changes the opportunity from selling applications based on how many people use them toward capturing a portion of the productivity and economic output those applications generate, which is where I believe Palantir becomes particularly interesting. 

The biggest bottleneck in enterprise AI is no longer necessarily the intelligence of the underlying model, but its ability to understand how a business actually operates including the relationships between its assets, suppliers, employees, permissions and operational constraints and that institutional knowledge cannot simply be purchased through an API, which is why I think Ontology could become one of the most valuable layers of the AI economy by connecting intelligence to the actual operating environment of an organization and allowing decisions to translate into real actions.

What makes this architecture particularly powerful is that every additional workflow integrated into Ontology potentially makes the surrounding system more valuable, because the relationships, permissions and operational decisions established through one application can become the foundation for automating additional processes across the organization. 

Over time that creates a compounding advantage where customers become increasingly dependent on the platform as more of their operations run through it, while the cost and complexity of replacing that infrastructure continue increasing where I think this becomes even more important as foundation models get cheaper and increasingly interchangeable, because lower intelligence costs should make thousands of additional workflows economical to automate, but every one of those agents still needs access to proprietary information, institutional context and a controlled way to execute decisions. 

Palantir doesn't need to develop smartest model in the world if it can become the operating environment underneath whichever models enterprises choose to deploy and the implications could extend well beyond traditional software budgets since a manufacturer increasing production without building another factory or an airline reducing costly maintenance downtime can generate enormous financial value, which creates an opportunity for Palantir to capture a meaningful portion of those improvements. 

The distinction is that creating value does not automatically mean capturing it, so the long-term opportunity ultimately depends on whether Palantir can prove that its platform delivers outcomes customers cannot easily replicate elsewhere and I think the financial results are already providing some of the strongest evidence that this model is working

What makes that particularly interesting is how Palantir's business model could evolve as its bootcamp distribution strategy and AI forward deployed engineering capabilities reduce the time and specialized labor required to build additional applications, potentially allowing the company to combine the switching costs of deeply integrated enterprise infrastructure with the scalability of traditional software. 

The company really doesn't need to monopolize enterprise AI but it does need to demonstrate that its ability to connect fragmented systems and execute complex operational workflows remains sufficiently differentiated to support continued expansion and pricing power which is why I believe Palantir has a credible path toward becoming one of the world's most valuable companies although I think investors need to separate the magnitude of that opportunity from what the current valuation already assumes. 

Intelligence will become increasingly abundant so the scarce and valuable layer may be the infrastructure that allows thousands of AI agents to understand, coordinate and safely execute decisions across the real economy so if that transition plays out the way I expect then Palantir has the potential to become much more than another enterprise software company because it could become one of the foundational operating layers of the autonomous enterprise which is exactly why I believe it has a legitimate opportunity to become one of most valuable companies in the world.

full_text_zh:
为什么 $PLTR 能够成为世界上最有价值的公司

我认为投资者在 Palantir 上犯的最大错误之一是继续通过传统的企业软件框架来评估公司，因为让这个机会对我来说如此有趣的是人工智能可以从根本上改变价值最终被捕获的地方。

几十年来，公司购买软件来帮助员工更有效地完成工作，但我认为我们正在接近一个更大的转变，软件越来越多地从协助人类决策转向在整个组织中自主执行决策，这改变了机会，从基于有多少人使用它们来销售应用程序，转向获取这些应用程序产生的部分生产力和经济产出，这就是我认为 Palantir 变得特别有趣的地方。

企业AI最大的瓶颈不再一定是底层模型的智能，而是它能够理解企业实际运营的能力，包括资产、供应商、员工、权限和运营约束之间的关系，而机构知识不能简单地通过API购买，这就是为什么我认为本体可以通过将智能与组织的实际运营环境连接起来并让决策转化为实际行动，成为AI经济中最有价值的层之一。

这种架构特别强大的原因在于，集成到本体中的每个额外工作流程都可能使周围系统变得更有价值，因为通过一个应用程序建立的关系、权限和操作决策可以成为整个组织中自动化额外流程的基础。

随着时间的推移，这会产生一种复合优势，随着越来越多的操作通过该平台运行，客户变得越来越依赖该平台，而更换基础设施的成本和复杂性不断增加，我认为随着基础模型变得更便宜且可互换性越来越高，这一点变得更加重要，因为较低的情报成本应该使数千个额外的工作流程能够经济地实现自动化，但每个代理仍然需要访问专有信息、机构背景和受控方式来执行决策。

如果 Palantir 能够成为企业选择部署的任何模型下的操作环境，那么 Palantir 就不需要开发世界上最智能的模型，而且其影响可能远远超出传统的软件预算，因为制造商在不建造另一家工厂的情况下提高产量，或者减少航空公司减少昂贵的维护停机时间，可以产生巨大的财务价值，这为 Palantir 创造了从这些改进中获得有意义的部分的机会。

区别在于，创造价值并不意味着自动获取价值，因此长期机会最终取决于 Palantir 能否证明其平台提供的成果是客户在其他地方无法轻易复制的，我认为财务业绩已经提供了一些最有力的证据，证明该模式正在发挥作用

特别有趣的是，Palantir 的业务模式将如何发展，因为其训练营分发策略和 AI 前向部署的工程能力减少了构建其他应用程序所需的时间和专业劳动力，从而有可能使该公司将深度集成的企业基础设施的转换成本与传统软件的可扩展性结合起来。

该公司确实不需要垄断企业人工智能，但它确实需要证明其连接分散系统和执行复杂操作工作流程的能力仍然具有足够的差异化，以支持持续扩张和定价能力，这就是为什么我相信Palantir有一条可靠的道路成为世界上最有价值的公司之一，尽管我认为投资者需要将这一机会的大小与当前估值已经假设的分开。

情报将变得越来越丰富，因此稀缺和有价值的层可能是允许数千个人工智能代理在实体经济中理解、协调和安全执行决策的基础设施，因此如果这种转变按照我预期的方式进行，那么 Palantir 有潜力成为比另一家企业软件公司更强大的公司，因为它可能成为自主企业的基础运营层之一，这正是我相信它有合法机会成为世界上最有价值的公司之一的原因。

title: ‼️ Anthropic has told Claude Code to stop recreating existing video games, even if they are renamed or called original.
title_en:
‼️ Anthropic has told Claude Code to stop recreating existing video games, even if they are renamed or called original.

The two-sentence rule appeared around 27 October on Opus 5.5. The X user who spotted it says it comes from Anthropic's servers and cannot be switched off.

Anthropic's Addy Osmani says using Claude to infringe IP already breaks its usage policy. Original games, genre games and games built from your own designs and assets should keep working.

It lands as indie studios such as Moonlighter maker Digital Sun hold back public playtests, afraid AI tools will clone their games before launch.

Osmani says anyone whose own work Claude turns down should "send it my way".
title_zh:
️ Anthropic 已告诉 Claude Code 停止重新创建现有的视频游戏，即使它们被重命名或称为原创游戏。

full_text_en:
‼️ Anthropic has told Claude Code to stop recreating existing video games, even if they are renamed or called original.

The two-sentence rule appeared around 27 October on Opus 5.5. The X user who spotted it says it comes from Anthropic's servers and cannot be switched off.

Anthropic's Addy Osmani says using Claude to infringe IP already breaks its usage policy. Original games, genre games and games built from your own designs and assets should keep working.

It lands as indie studios such as Moonlighter maker Digital Sun hold back public playtests, afraid AI tools will clone their games before launch.

Osmani says anyone whose own work Claude turns down should "send it my way".

️ Anthropic 已告诉 Claude Code 停止重新创建现有的视频游戏，即使它们被重命名或称为原创游戏。

两句话规则于 10 月 27 日左右出现在 Opus 5.5 上。发现它的 X 用户表示它来自 Anthropic 的服务器并且无法关闭。

Anthropic 的 Addy Osmani 表示，利用 Claude 侵犯知识产权已经违反了其使用政策。原创游戏、类型游戏以及根据您自己的设计和资产构建的游戏应该继续运行。

由于担心人工智能工具会在发布前克隆他们的游戏，Moonlighter 制造商 Digital Sun 等独立工作室推迟了公开游戏测试。

title_en:
Remove your main @github account from your computer. Now.

Give your AI agent a separate GitHub account with minimal permissions per repo.

Let the agent create PRs, then use your main account to review and merge them.

Obvious advice, but essential in the age of AI agents.
title_zh:
从计算机中删除您的主 @github 帐户。现在。

为您的 AI 代理提供一个单独的 GitHub 帐户，每个存储库具有最小的权限。

让代理创建 PR，然后使用您的主帐户来审查和合并它们。

显而易见的建议，但在人工智能代理时代至关重要

title: The frustration with UVA football is real, but the core problem is larger than any player, coach or single individual. I
title_en:
The frustration with UVA football is real, but the core problem is larger than any player, coach or single individual. In my view, it is a business problem.

Charlottesville (where one of our Good Feet stores resides) is one of the smallest TV markets in the country. Athletics today run on multi-year brand deals, NIL collectives, and revenue flywheels from large alumni bases and proximity to major corporate HQs. UVA lacks the geographical advantages and lacks the scale and reach of Ohio State, Michigan, Texas, or Florida. That is a structural constraint.

UVA’s football fan base is more fragile (not a fault of fans) due to a lack of a winning tradition compared to the power programs—Alabama, Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio State, Michigan, USC. Those are the Amazon, Walmarts and Coca-Colas of college football. They can operate on tradition and confidence that their customers will be back even when they miss. UVA cannot afford many misses and has to be scrappy: more creative, more personal, and more deliberate about every fan, donor, and sponsor. Otherwise the support of the fan base erodes quickly. The football program would make a strong Darden case study on building without the giants’ natural advantages.

In 2021 we were early NIL partners with UVA. We started with Kihei Clark on TV spots, then expanded to other athletes in UVA-logo jerseys, attaching millions in Good Feet advertising to the UVA brand. We followed the university’s approach: not pay-to-play, but real marketing leverage, inviting players to conferences, networking, and speaking opportunities. We did the same for others in football, men’s and women’s basketball, and non-rev sports. We are not a major Fortune 500 brand but we have made meaningful investments and will match our heart with anyone.

Two years ago major money flowed into UVA football. Problem solved, or so it seemed! Emphasis seemed to shift to seven and eight-figure checks. Those are wonderful gifts but that is not a sustainable model. Amazon, Coca-Cola, and Walmart, built flywheels one customer at a time.

Is it possible that those generous donations muddied good strategic thinking? It seems there is need of a strategy that attaches value at every level: the single fan with family at a few games, season-ticket holders and lower-level donors, small businesses attaching to the brand, larger sponsors, mid-tier five- and six-figure donors, and the premium seven-to-eight figure donors. When you are customer focused, you are accountable to those customers. Is it possible, that greater accountability to customers up and down the ladder, could foster better football strategy?

Tradition and humility can go together; tradition and entitlement cannot. Academic excellence and history are strengths, not automatic equalizers to the football powers. Be accountable to the people paying the bills, make hard, strategic decisions, be creative, listen. Embrace being David because you will never be Goliath. Winning will come.

full_text_zh:
弗吉尼亚大学足球队的挫败感是真实存在的，但核心问题比任何球员、教练或个人都更大。在我看来，这是一个商业问题。

夏洛茨维尔（我们的 Good Feet 商店之一就坐落于此）是美国最小的电视市场之一。如今的田径运动依赖于多年的品牌交易、NIL 集体以及来自大型校友基地和靠近主要公司总部的收入飞轮。 UVA 缺乏地理优势，也缺乏俄亥俄州、密歇根州、德克萨斯州或佛罗里达州的规模和覆盖范围。这是一个结构性限制。

与阿拉巴马州、德克萨斯州、俄克拉荷马州、俄亥俄州、密歇根州、南加州大学等实力项目相比，UVA 的橄榄球迷基础更加脆弱（不是球迷的错），因为缺乏获胜传统。这些是大学橄榄球界的亚马逊、沃尔玛和可口可乐。他们可以秉承传统经营，并相信即使顾客错过了，他们也会回来。 UVA 不能承受太多的失误，必须斗志昂扬：更有创意、更个性化、对每一位粉丝、捐助者和赞助商都更加深思熟虑。否则粉丝群的支持很快就会消失。足球项目将为达顿在没有巨人队天然优势的情况下进行建设提供强有力的案例研究。

2021 年，我们成为 UVA 的早期 NIL 合作伙伴。我们首先在电视广告中让基黑·克拉克 (Kihei Clark) 上场，然后扩展到穿着 UVA 徽标球衣的其他运动员，为 UVA 品牌投放了数百万美元的 Good Feet 广告。我们遵循了大学的方法：不是付费游戏，而是真正的营销杠杆，邀请玩家参加会议、社交和演讲机会。我们对足球、男子和女子篮球以及非职业体育运动中的其他人也做了同样的事情。我们不是财富 500 强的主要品牌，但我们进行了有意义的投资，并将与任何人心心相印。

两年前，大量资金流入弗吉尼亚大学橄榄球队。问题解决了，至少看起来是这样！重点似乎转向七位数和八位数的支票。这些都是很棒的礼物，但这不是一个可持续的模式。亚马逊、可口可乐和沃尔玛一次为一位客户制造飞轮。

这些慷慨的捐赠是否有可能混淆了良好的战略思维？似乎需要一种在各个层面赋予价值的策略：与家人一起观看几场比赛的单一球迷、季票持有者和较低级别的捐赠者、依附于品牌的小型企业、较大的赞助商、中型五位数和六位数的捐赠者以及高级七到八位数的捐赠者。当您以客户为中心时，您就要对这些客户负责。对上下级客户承担更大的责任是否有可能促进更好的足球战略？

传统与谦逊可以并存；传统和权利不能。卓越的学术成就和历史是优势，而不是足球强国的自动均衡器。对支付账单的人负责，做出艰难的战略决策，发挥创造力，倾听。拥抱成为大卫，因为你永远不会成为歌利亚。胜利将会到来。

title: Claude Code found 17,342 of my daughter's photos on a server in Hangzhou. she's 16. she had her Hidden album locked with
title_en:
Claude Code found 17,342 of my daughter's photos on a server in Hangzhou. she's 16. she had her Hidden album locked with Face ID and thought nobody could see it. an app she downloaded from the App Store has been sending every photo on her phone to China for 10 months. i checked her two friends' phones the same night. same app. same server.

her phone was lagging so i connected it to my MacBook. Claude Code flagged an app called "GlowCam - Beauty Filter" with 4.2 million downloads. it was uploading her entire photo library every 6 hours between 1am and 5am while she was sleeping.

→ app → "GlowCam - Beauty Filter" (4.2M downloads, 4.7 stars)
→ server → 112.17.***.63
→ location → Hangzhou, China
→ total files uploaded → 17,342
→ active since → January 2026
→ permissions → camera, photos, microphone, location

every photo she ever took. every screenshot. every image anyone ever sent her. everything from her Hidden album that she locked with Face ID thinking it was safe. Face ID only stops a person who picks up the phone. an app with Full Access to Photos opens the Hidden album like any other folder. there's no green dot for that.

two of her friends were at our house that evening. i asked them to let me check their phones. both had GlowCam installed.

→ my daughter's iPhone 16 Pro Max → 17,342 files uploaded to Hangzhou
→ her friend's iPhone 15 → 9,740 files uploaded to the same server
→ her friend's iPhone 15 → 6,210 files uploaded since April

3 phones on my kitchen table all sending photos to the same folder in China.

i asked Claude Code to trace where the files went. it found photos from all 3 phones on a site that sells stolen photo libraries sorted by age and location.

→ www.le***dumpcc → their city listed, folders tagged "16-19"
→ tme/ph***vault_cn (41,000+ subscribers) → folder link shared 2 weeks ago
→ buyer access → $8 per library

someone paid $8 per library. 3 libraries from 3 teenage girls. Apple approved the app that made it possible.

then Claude Code scanned every other app on all 3 phones and found 2 more doing the same thing.

→ "PhotoRoom — Background Eraser" → uploading to a server in Jakarta
→ "FaceTune Lite — Selfie Editor" → uploading to a server in Mumbai

what Claude Code did on all 3 phones:

→ killed every upload process and purged all caches
→ revoked Full Access from every photo app
→ switched everything to "Limited Access"
→ filed DMCA takedowns on the site and the telegram channel
→ turned on Advanced Data Protection for iCloud on all 3 accounts

the site took the photos down in 72 hours. the telegram channel is still up.

i called both their parents that night. i told all 3 girls the apps were slowing their phones and i deleted them. none of them know what i actually found.

if your kid has a beauty filter or photo editor on their phone right now there's a real chance it's doing exactly this. check Settings → Privacy & Security → Photos and count how many apps have "Full Access." every single one can read the Hidden album, the Recently Deleted folder, and every photo your kid has ever taken.

my daughter had 11 apps with Full Access. she needed 2.

the prompt is in the first reply. run it on every phone in your house tonight. takes 3 minutes. save it and send it to every parent you know.

full_text_zh:
Claude Code 在杭州的一台服务器上找到了 17,342 张我女儿的照片。她 16 岁。她用 Face ID 锁定了她的隐藏相册，并认为没有人可以看到它。她从 App Store 下载的一个应用程序已经将她手机上的所有照片发送到中国 10 个月了。当天晚上我检查了她两个朋友的手机。相同的应用程序。同一个服务器。

她的手机出现延迟，所以我将其连接到我的 MacBook。 Claude Code 标记了一款名为“GlowCam - Beauty Filter”的应用程序，下载量为 420 万次。当她睡觉时，它会在凌晨 1 点到 5 点之间每 6 小时上传一次她的整个照片库。

→ 应用程序 →“GlowCam - 美颜滤镜”（420 万次下载，4.7 星）
→ 服务器 → 112.17.***.63
→ 地点 → 中国杭州
→ 上传文件总数 → 17,342
→ 自 2026 年 1 月起生效
→ 权限 → 相机、照片、麦克风、位置

她拍的每张照片。每一张截图。任何人发给她的每张照片。她用 Face ID 锁定的隐藏相册中的所有内容都被认为是安全的。 Face ID 只会阻止拿起电话的人。具有对照片的完全访问权限的应用程序可以像任何其他文件夹一样打开隐藏相册。没有绿点。

那天晚上她的两个朋友在我们家。我要求他们让我检查他们的手机。两者都安装了 GlowCam。

→ 我女儿的 iPhone 16 Pro Max → 17,342 个文件上传到杭州
→ 她朋友的 iPhone 15 → 9,740 个文件上传到同一服务器
→ 她朋友的 iPhone 15 → 自 4 月份以来上传了 6,210 个文件

我厨房桌子上的 3 部手机都将照片发送到中国的同一个文件夹。

我要求 Claude Code 追踪文件的去向。它在一个出售被盗照片库的网站上发现了所有 3 部手机中的照片，这些照片按年龄和地点排序。

→ www.le***dumpcc → 列出了他们的城市，文件夹标记为“16-19”
→ tme/ph***vault_cn（41,000+ 订阅者）→ 两周前共享的文件夹链接
→ 买家访问权限 → 每个图书馆 8 美元

有人为每个图书馆支付了 8 美元。 3 个少女的 3 个图书馆。苹果批准了这款应用程序，使之成为可能。

然后 Claude Code 扫描了所有 3 部手机上的所有其他应用程序，发现另外 2 个应用程序在做同样的事情。

→“PhotoRoom — 背景橡皮擦”→上传到雅加达的服务器
→“FaceTune Lite — 自拍编辑器”→ 上传到孟买的服务器

Claude Code 在所有 3 部手机上做了什么：

→ 终止所有上传进程并清除所有缓存
→ 撤销所有照片应用程序的完全访问权限
→ 将所有内容切换为“受限访问”
→ 在网站和电报频道上提交 DMCA 删除
→ 在所有 3 个帐户上启用 iCloud 高级数据保护

该网站在 72 小时内删除了这些照片。电报频道仍然正常。

那天晚上我给他们的父母打电话。我告诉所有 3 个女孩这些应用程序降低了她们的手机速度，然后我删除了它们。他们都不知道我到底发现了什么。

如果您的孩子现在手机上有美颜滤镜或照片编辑器，那么它很有可能就是这样做的。检查“设置”→“隐私和安全”→“照片”并计算有多少个应用程序具有“完全访问权限”。每个人都可以阅读隐藏相册、最近删除的文件夹以及您孩子拍摄的每张照片。

我女儿有 11 个具有完全访问权限的应用程序。她需要2个。

提示在第一个回复中。今晚在你家里的每部手机上运行它。需要 3 分钟。保存它并将其发送给您认识的每一位家长。

title: We're only in the second or third innings of this massive AI infrastructure buildout and we're not going to see the full
title_en:
We're only in the second or third innings of this massive AI infrastructure buildout and we're not going to see the full profitability of these investments until the eighth or ninth inning.

One of the biggest concerns on Wall Street right now is the enormous amount of capital being poured into AI. Companies like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta are spending and raising hundreds of billions of dollars building data centers and I fully expect some of these companies to experience negative free cash flow for the next couple years as they continue ramping up their capital expenditures. But I don't necessarily think that's a bad thing, especially when you consider the scale of the opportunity ahead.

We're essentially watching the construction of an entirely new computing infrastructure, and building that infrastructure requires enormous upfront investments before the full economic benefits become visible. Think about it. We're still in the earliest stages of AI agents, autonomous systems, enterprise AI adoption, and advanced reasoning models. As these technologies become more capable and widely adopted, the demand for computing power will increase dramatically.

The important distinction is that the spending happens today, while much of the potential profitability may not materialize until years down the road. That's what makes this investment cycle so difficult for Wall Street to evaluate. Investors are looking at declining free cash flow and questioning whether these companies are spending too aggressively, while the companies themselves are preparing for demand they believe will be substantially larger in the future. Of course, there's no guarantee that every company will earn an attractive return on these investments. Some will overspend, some will struggle with execution, and others will emerge as major winners. But I think it's a mistake to judge a multiyear infrastructure buildout solely by the negative cash flow we're seeing during its earliest stages.

Thanks for having me on the show, @cvpayne! Always a pleasure discussing the markets and the incredible opportunities ahead in AI.

我们只处于大规模人工智能基础设施建设的第二或第三局，直到第八或第九局我们才会看到这些投资的全部盈利能力。

目前华尔街最大的担忧之一是大量资金涌入人工智能领域。微软、亚马逊、谷歌和 Meta 等公司正在花费和筹集数千亿美元建设数据中心，我完全预计其中一些公司在未来几年将经历负自由现金流，因为他们将继续增加资本支出。但我并不认为这是一件坏事，特别是当你考虑到未来机会的规模时。

我们实质上正在关注全新计算基础设施的建设，而建设该基础设施需要大量的前期投资才能看到全部经济效益。想一想。我们仍处于人工智能代理、自治系统、企业人工智能采用和高级推理模型的最早阶段。随着这些技术变得越来越强大并被广泛采用，对计算能力的需求将急剧增加。

重要的区别在于，支出发生在今天，而大部分潜在的盈利能力可能要几年后才能实现。这就是华尔街难以评估这一投资周期的原因。投资者正在关注自由现金流的下降，并质疑这些公司的支出是否过于激进，而这些公司本身正在为他们认为未来会大幅增长的需求做好准备。当然，并不能保证每家公司都能从这些投资中获得可观的回报。有些人会超支，有些人会在执行上遇到困难，还有一些人会成为主要赢家。但我认为，仅根据我们在早期阶段看到的负现金流来判断多年基础设施建设是错误的。

感谢您邀请我参加节目，@cvpayne！总是很高兴讨论市场和人工智能未来的难以置信的机遇。

title_en:
LLMs accumulate a lot of declarative knowledge.
That's how they can answer a large number of questions. 
That's also why they require so many parameters and hence so much memory. 

But one can replace the accumulation of knowledge by *understanding*
That what JEPA world models do. 
That's one reason they can be useful with considerably less memory and training data  than LLMs.

title: New Meta, NYU paper shows that a simple loop with good Lean tools and more compute matches or beats hand-built theorem-p
title_en:
New Meta, NYU paper shows that a simple loop with good Lean tools and more compute matches or beats hand-built theorem-proving workflows.

Systems that write math proofs in Lean, a language a computer can check, increasingly use hand-designed workflows that plan and split up problems. Their gains often come with stronger models or more compute, hiding what the workflow adds.

They built h1, a loop that gives the model fast Lean feedback and search tools, and keeps it working after each failed check. It imposes no plan, only a progress summary before each new round.

With the same model, h1 beat the hand-built Goedel-Architect on PutnamBench, 598 problems to 597, at $1.08 against $1.47 per problem. The interface still matters: with Opus 4.8, h1 solved 83 of 100 hard algebra problems, against 63 for Claude Code.

title: this is f*cking insane. andrej karpathy: "the biggest regret of every engineer in my field right now is every AI convers
title_en:
this is f*cking insane. andrej karpathy: "the biggest regret of every engineer in my field right now is every AI conversation they never saved, and in 10 years the ones who started saving in 2024 will be running circles around the rest of us"

andrej karpathy, co-founder of openai, pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain that remembers every article, pdf, transcript and conversation you ever fed it

you point claude code at a folder, drop anything into it, and claude reads it, cross-links it with everything already there, and writes it into a living wiki. your knowledge finally compounds instead of leaking out of your head every friday

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault
→ run claude in that folder and type "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
→ drop any file into /raw (youtube transcript, meeting notes, 400-page pdf, screenshot of a tweet) and type "ingest"
→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones automatically, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it noticed about how you think
→ never open a blank claude chat again. every question goes through the vault, every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to set up. compounding knowledge from that evening forward

the ugly part most will scroll past: in 10 years the engineers who started this in 2024 will remember every book, every podcast, every meeting with receipts. you will remember none of them. karpathy already picked which side he is on and you are still not on his

My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!

I copied the video clips from my DJI to a folder, then ope
title_en:
My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!

I copied the video clips from my DJI to a folder, then opened Claude Code in it and asked it to edit it into a 10 minute vlog

I made a few adjustments but not a lot

It transcribed everything I said with mlx-whisper (Whisper large-v3-turbo running on my MacBook Pro's GPU through Apple's MLX)

It pulled video frames every few seconds into grid images (contact sheets), so Claude could see what's in each clip

It used SpeechBrain ECAPA (a voice-matching model) to figure out what was my voice from other people

It then made thumbnails with OpenCV with YuNet's face detector

The edit itself is a list of cuts in a JSON file: which clip, start time, end time, Claude then picked the pieces by reading the transcripts and looking at the frame grids by itself

I added on screen captions for X and on YouTube for the first minute with Pillow (Python's image library)

P.S. I didn't ask for any of this, and I didn't know any of this until @thesamparr just asked me how I edited it

All I asked for was "Claude can you edit these clips into a 10 minute vlog for X and YouTube"

I think if I didn't have AI to edit it, I wouldn't be vlogging because editing would be such a painful and slow process for me and hiring someone to do it would be even more hassle for me!

它转录了我用 mlx-whisper 所说的一切（Whisper large-v3-turbo 通过 Apple 的 MLX 在我的 MacBook Pro 的 GPU 上运行）

然后使用 OpenCV 和 YuNet 的人脸检测器制作缩略图

编辑本身是 JSON 文件中的剪辑列表：哪个剪辑、开始时间、结束时间，然后 Claude 通过阅读脚本并自行查看帧网格来挑选片段

我使用 Pillow（Python 的图像库）在 X 的屏幕标题和 YouTube 上添加了第一分钟的标题

附：我没有要求任何这些，我也不知道这些，直到 @thesamparr 只是问我如何编辑它

我所要求的只是“克劳德，你能将这些剪辑编辑成 X 和 YouTube 的 10 分钟视频博客吗”

我想如果我没有人工智能来编辑它，我就不会做视频博客，因为编辑对我来说是一个痛苦而缓慢的过程，而且雇人来做这对我来说会更麻烦！

附：我没有要求任何这些，我也不知道这些，直到 @thesamparr 只是问我如何编辑它

我所要求的只是“克劳德，你能将这些剪辑编辑成 X 和 YouTube 的 10 分钟视频博客吗”

我想如果我没有人工智能来编辑它，我就不会做视频博客，因为编辑对我来说是一个痛苦而缓慢的过程，而且雇人来做这对我来说会更麻烦！

title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
title_en:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

full_text_zh:
周末黑客：HackerTube。我对 YouTube 的推荐感到恼火，因此我让 Claude 将 HN 20 年来的 4300 万条评论过滤为 6,454 个不断推荐的视频。 *显着*更好的观看体验，Opus 5.5 约 2 小时：

- 无需任何登录即可获得出色的记录（状态保存在本地浏览器会话中）
- 缩略图是视频中间的代表性帧，而不是超级骗子 A/B 测试超优化的用户上传
- 来自评论分析的基础数据作为一个 zip 文件，将你的 Claude 指向它并询问你自己的版本
- HackerTube 长 ✊

更多关于该过程的信息：
我使用 Claude Code（Mac 桌面应用程序）、中等工作量的 Opus 5.5 作为我的默认设置。我只与 Claude 交谈并让它完成所有工作，我协同帮助的唯一“手动工作”是在浏览器中（让人想起 MenuGen）：1）我必须从 Google Cloud UI 创建某种 API 密钥来查询 YouTube 的视频元数据，2）我启动了一个 VPS 盒子进行服务，3）我购买了域名。盒子启动后，我给了 Claude IP，并告诉它更新、保护、强化、部署和优化代码，它完成了全部工作。

许多原本需要数周/数月才能完成的精彩项目现在甚至可以在早餐时就完成。还有什么是我们没有想到的。

title:
🚨 PARASITE EVE II (1999) HAS BEEN PORTED NATIVELY TO PC — WITH 60 FPS, HIGHER RESOLUTIONS & MOD SUPPORT! 🧟🔥

One of the
title_en:
🚨 PARASITE EVE II (1999) HAS BEEN PORTED NATIVELY TO PC — WITH 60 FPS, HIGHER RESOLUTIONS & MOD SUPPORT! 🧟🔥

One of the PlayStation's most beloved survival-horror RPGs is now PLAYABLE on Windows thanks to an incredible fan-made native PC port! 🎮

Developer Snaity (Adriano Teodoro) has brought Square's PS1 classic to modern PCs using the original game's decompiled C code, building upon the work of GabeRealB and contributors!

And this isn't conventional PlayStation emulation!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS PC PORT — NO PS1 EMULATOR REQUIRED!

The original PlayStation game code has been compiled for PC, with a custom runtime handling graphics, sound, controllers and other console functionality!

✅ HIGHER RESOLUTIONS — UP TO 8X THE ORIGINAL!

GPU-accelerated rendering with sub-pixel precision, perspective-correct textures and improved 3D image stability!

✅ SMOOTH 60 FPS PRESENTATION!

The original game logic continues running at 30 FPS, while interpolated frames deliver smoother 60 FPS visuals without adding input delay!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS!

Camera-relative analogue movement, remappable controls and modern gamepad support, alongside the original tank controls!

✅ ENHANCED VISUALS!

Bilinear texture filtering, bicubic background scaling, sharper HD text, optional CRT effects and integer scaling!

✅ EXPERIMENTAL MOD SUPPORT!

Replace backgrounds, textures, music, movies and game text! Translation support, cheats and asset extraction tools are also included!

🎮 BOTH DISCS PLAYABLE!

The port supports both discs, including cinematics, music, sound effects, saving and controller functionality.

💾 SAVE COMPATIBILITY!

Memory-card files can be transferred between the PC port and DuckStation!

🖥️ A GENUINE NATIVE PC PORT!

Unlike an emulator-based wrapper, PE2PC runs the game's decompiled code natively, with a custom Rust-based PC runtime replacing the PlayStation's hardware services.

⚠️ REQUIREMENTS:

💿 Your own USA PlayStation game dumps (SLUS-01042 and SLUS-01055), in CHD or CUE format.

💻 Windows 10/11 with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 support.

No copyrighted game data is included.

🛠️ CREDITS:

Developed by Snaity (Adriano Teodoro), building upon GabeRealB's Parasite Eve II decompilation.

🤖 AI DEVELOPMENT DISCLOSURE:

The developer openly credits Claude Code for writing much of the project's code, tools and documentation, with Snaity directing, reviewing and testing the work.

⭐ Please consider starring the GitHub repository to support development!

🚨 《寄生虫前夜 II》(1999) 已原生移植到 PC — 具有 60 FPS、更高的分辨率和 MOD 支持！ 🧟🔥

PlayStation 最受欢迎的生存恐怖角色扮演游戏之一现在可以在 Windows 上玩，这要归功于令人难以置信的粉丝制作的原生 PC 移植！ 🎮

开发人员 Snaity（阿德里亚诺·特奥多罗）在 GabeRealB 和贡献者的工作基础上，使用原始游戏的反编译 C 代码，将 Square 的 PS1 经典游戏带入了现代 PC！

这不是传统的 PlayStation 模拟！

🔥 特点：

✅ 原生 WINDOWS PC 端口 — 无需 PS1 模拟器！

原始 PlayStation 游戏代码已针对 PC 进行编译，具有自定义运行时处理图形、声音、控制器和其他控制台功能！

✅ 更高的分辨率 — 高达原始分辨率的 8 倍！

GPU 加速渲染具有亚像素精度、透视校正纹理和改进的 3D 图像稳定性！

✅ 流畅的 60 FPS 演示！

原始游戏逻辑继续以 30 FPS 运行，而插值帧可提供更流畅的 60 FPS 视觉效果，而不会增加输入延迟！

✅ 现代控制！

与摄像机相关的模拟运动、可重新映射的控件和现代游戏手柄支持，以及原始的坦克控件！

✅ 增强视觉效果！

双线性纹理过滤、双三次背景缩放、更清晰的高清文本、可选的 CRT 效果和整数缩放！

✅ 实验性模组支持！

替换背景、纹理、音乐、电影和游戏文本！还包括翻译支持、作弊和资产提取工具！

🎮 两张光盘都可以播放！

该端口支持两种光盘，包括电影、音乐、音效、保存和控制器功能。

💾 保存兼容性！

存储卡文件可以在 PC 端口和 DuckStation 之间传输！

🖥️ 真正的原生 PC 端口！

与基于模拟器的包装器不同，PE2PC 原生运行游戏的反编译代码，并使用基于 Rust 的自定义 PC 运行时替换 PlayStation 的硬件服务。

⚠️要求：

💿 您自己的美国 PlayStation 游戏转储（SLUS-01042 和 SLUS-01055），采用 CHD 或 CUE 格式。

💻 支持 Vulkan 或 OpenGL 3.3 的 Windows 10/11。

不包含受版权保护的游戏数据。

🛠️ 制作人员：

由 Snaity (Adriano Teodoro) 开发，基于 GabeRealB 的 Parasite Eve II 反编译。

🤖 AI 开发披露：

开发人员公开承认 Claude Code 编写了该项目的大部分代码、工具和文档，并由 Snaity 指导、审查和测试了这些工作。

title: So many people keep complaining about the CapEx at $META $AMZN $GOOGL and $MSFT without looking at what these businesses
title_en:
So many people keep complaining about the CapEx at $META $AMZN $GOOGL and $MSFT without looking at what these businesses are actually producing.

You want faster growth, better products, more cloud capacity, and leadership in AI. Then the bill arrives for the infrastructure required to deliver it, and suddenly everyone wants management to stop spending.

Where exactly do you think that growth is supposed to come from?

Look at the operating cash flow chart. Over the trailing twelve months:

• $META: $133 billion, up 23.7%
• $AMZN: $168 billion, up 28.8%
• $GOOGL: $180 billion, up 18.6%
• $MSFT: $196 billion, up 33.2%
Combined, that’s approximately $677 BILLION in cash from operations. An increase of $140 billion, or 26.1%, in one year.

Anyone discussing their spending without acknowledging that growth is leaving out a pretty damn important part of the story.

Now look at the second chart. Combined CapEx increased from approximately $330 billion to $615 billion.

Of course that puts pressure on free cash flow. When investment spending grows faster than operating cash generation, less cash is left over. That arithmetic tells you how much cash remains after investment. By itself, it doesn’t tell you whether management is making a good investment.

A business generating substantial cash and reinvesting aggressively deserves a different analysis from a business whose operations cannot support themselves.

Amazon is a perfect example. Its reported trailing twelve-month free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion, while operating cash flow increased 29% to $168.3 billion. Meanwhile, AWS revenue grew 39%, and Amazon delivered its highest quarterly operating margin ever at 13.9%. Explain how “negative free cash flow” alone captures what is happening inside that business.

Microsoft reported Azure growth of 48% and quarterly operating cash flow of $58 billion. Management still says customer demand exceeds available supply. When customers want more capacity than you can provide, building capacity is a pretty logical business decision.

Google Cloud revenue increased 103% to $30.7 billion, with operating income climbing from approximately $3.6 billion to $11.1 billion. Infrastructure and enterprise AI demand contributed to that growth, alongside TPU systems sales. There is an actual business developing here with actual customers and actual operating profits.

Meta says its AI investments are already generating additional advertising revenue through better recommendations, stronger engagement, and improved monetization. That matters because AI can improve the economics of products billions of people already use, well before some entirely new business becomes material.

This is the relationship investors need to understand: infrastructure enables more usage, better products, and additional revenue opportunities. Successful investments can expand cash generation, which helps fund the next round of growth.

The money goes out before the full benefit comes back. A data center doesn’t repay its construction cost the quarter it opens.

That doesn’t make every dollar of CapEx brilliant. These charts alone cannot prove that spending caused every dollar of cash flow growth. Equipment depreciates, operating costs rise, and management still has to earn an adequate return.

Hold them accountable for that. Look at demand, utilization, margins, and the cash those assets generate over time. I absolutely care about free cash flow, including whether today’s spending eventually produces more of it.

What I’m tired of is people treating a lower free cash flow number as the entire investment thesis while ignoring the expanding businesses underneath it.

You can make this year’s free cash flow look better by cutting investment. You can also leave yourself without the capacity to serve next year’s customers.

I want management building a more profitable, more competitive business for the next decade.

If your entire analysis ends at “CapEx went up,” you haven’t finished the analysis.

full_text_zh:
很多人一直抱怨 $META $AMZN $GOOGL 和 $MSFT 的资本支出，却没有关注这些企业实际生产的产品。

您想要更快的增长、更好的产品、更多的云容量以及人工智能领域的领先地位。然后，交付所需的基础设施账单到了，突然每个人都希望管理层停止支出。

您认为增长到底应该来自哪里？

看看经营现金流量表。过去十二个月：

• $META：1,330 亿美元，增长 23.7%
• 亚马逊：1,680 亿美元，增长 28.8%
• $GOOGL：1800 亿美元，增长 18.6%
• $MSFT：1,960 亿美元，增长 33.2%
合计起来，运营现金约为 6,770 亿美元。一年内增加了1400亿美元，即26.1%。

任何人在讨论支出而不承认增长的情况下都会遗漏故事中非常重要的部分。

现在看第二张图表。合并资本支出从约 3,300 亿美元增加至 6,150 亿美元。

当然，这会给自由现金流带来压力。当投资支出增长快于经营性现金生成时，剩余现金就会减少。该算术告诉您投资后还剩下多少现金。它本身并不能告诉你管理层是否做出了良好的投资。

产生大量现金并积极进行再投资的企业应该与运营无法自给自足的企业进行不同的分析。

亚马逊就是一个完美的例子。据报道，过去 12 个月的自由现金流为负 424 亿美元，而运营现金流增长 29％，达到 1,683 亿美元。与此同时，AWS 收入增长了 39%，亚马逊实现了有史以来最高的季度运营利润率，达到 13.9%。解释“负自由现金流”如何单独反映该企业内部发生的情况。

微软公布 Azure 增长 48%，季度运营现金流达 580 亿美元。管理层仍然表示，客户需求超过了可用供应。当客户需要的容量超出您所能提供的容量时，构建容量是一个非常合乎逻辑的业务决策。

Google Cloud 收入增长 103%，达到 307 亿美元，营业收入从约 36 亿美元攀升至 111 亿美元。基础设施和企业人工智能需求以及 TPU 系统销售推动了这一增长。这里有实际的业务在发展，有实际的客户和实际的营业利润。

Meta 表示，其人工智能投资已经通过更好的推荐、更强的参与度和改善的货币化产生了额外的广告收入。这很重要，因为人工智能可以提高数十亿人已经使用的产品的经济性，早在一些全新的业务变得实质性之前。

这是投资者需要理解的关系：基础设施可以带来更多的使用、更好的产品和额外的收入机会。成功的投资可以扩大现金生成，从而为下一轮增长提供资金。

在全部收益回来之前，钱就花掉了。数据中心在开业时并不会偿还其建设成本。

这并不能让每一美元的资本支出都变得出色。仅凭这些图表并不能证明每一美元的现金流增长都是支出造成的。设备贬值，运营成本上升，管理层仍需获得足够的回报。

让他们为此负责。看看这些资产随着时间的推移产生的需求、利用率、利润率和现金。我绝对关心自由现金流，包括今天的支出最终是否会产生更多现金流。

我厌倦的是人们将较低的自由现金流数字视为整个投资主题，而忽略了其背后不断扩展的业务。

你可以通过削减投资来让今年的自由现金流看起来更好。您还可能导致自己没有能力为明年的客户提供服务。

我希望管理层在未来十年打造利润更高、竞争力更强的业务。

如果您的整个分析以“资本支出上升”结束，则您尚未完成分析。

title_en:
GitHub is blowing up with free skills that turn Claude Code into a video studio.

Here are 8 worth bookmarking if you're tired of paying for motion graphics:

1/ pixelfx 

244 hand-coded pixel effects: fire, explosions, magic, weather.

The skill makes Claude act like a fussy pixel artist. It draws, renders, checks and tweaks until the effect looks right.

https://t.co/MAr9nrztaC

2/ huashu-motion 
Ask for "a 30-second launch video for my product". It writes the script and picks the music.

Don't like a moment? Click that spot in the frame and it fixes only that bit.

https://t.co/rnEBvZTxq5

3/ mg-styles-15

15 motion graphics styles, each with a 10-second demo.

Every one was built by Opus 5.5. Prompts and source code included.

https://t.co/ndOfbksKQo

4/ motion-prompt 

A dictionary of 192 motion, camera and web effects.

Each one has a live example and the exact words to prompt it. Perfect when you know the look but not the name.

https://t.co/5JseyprmCJ

5/ animate 

Explainer shorts and mini stories, made in pure code.

7 styles built in: paper cut-out, pen hatching, stencil print, pixel art and more. Give it a reference image and it learns a new one.

https://t.co/JLuAsgCxKF

6/ vibe-knowledge-film

Viral Douyin-style knowledge shorts on autopilot.

Drop in a topic or script. It handles subtitles, storyboard and sound effects. You approve a 30-second sample before it builds the full cut.

https://t.co/iVOnc838pU

7/ story-studio 

Narrated history and character stories, start to finish.

Topic, script, voiceover and visuals, delivered as a CapCut draft you can open and edit.

https://t.co/xNg0Cm7YfL

8/ video-editor-skills

Rough cuts for vlogs and voiceovers inside DaVinci Resolve.

It removes retakes and pauses, then adds B-roll, music and subtitles. Needs paid DaVinci. Non-commercial use only.

https://t.co/Oy241KDXJb

That's the list.

Bookmark this so you have it when your next video is due.

full_text_zh:
GitHub 正在大量提供免费技能，将 Claude Code 转变为视频工作室。

如果您厌倦了为动态图形付费，这里有 8 个值得添加书签的内容：

1/ 像素特效

244 种手工编码的像素效果：火焰、爆炸、魔法、天气。

这项技能让克劳德表现得像一个挑剔的像素艺术家。它会进行绘制、渲染、检查和调整，直到效果看起来正确为止。

2/ 画数运动
要求“我的产品的 30 秒发布视频”。它编写剧本并选择音乐。

不喜欢一会儿吗？单击框架中的该点，它只会修复该位。

3/ 毫克-样式-15

15 种动态图形风格，每种风格都有 10 秒的演示。

每一件都是由 Opus 5.5 构建的。包括提示和源代码。

4/ 动作提示

包含 192 种动作、相机和网络效果的字典。

每个都有一个活生生的例子和提示它的确切单词。当您知道外观但不知道名称时，这是完美的。

5/ 动画

用纯代码制作的讲解短片和迷你故事。

内置 7 种样式：剪纸、钢笔阴影、模板印刷、像素艺术等。给它一张参考图像，它就会学习一张新图像。

6/ 氛围知识电影

自动驾驶仪上的病毒式抖音式知识短片。

放入主题或脚本。它处理字幕、故事板和声音效果。您先批准 30 秒的样本，然后再构建完整的剪辑。

7/ 故事工作室

从头到尾讲述历史和人物故事。

主题、脚本、旁白和视觉效果以 CapCut 草稿形式提供，您可以打开和编辑。

8/ 视频编辑技能

在 DaVinci Resolve 中对视频博客和配音进行粗剪。

它消除了重拍和暂停，然后添加了幕后花絮、音乐和字幕。需要付费达芬奇。仅限非商业用途。

这就是清单。

将此添加为书签，以便您在下一个视频到期时可以使用它。

title: Things are different in 2026 vs 2020, but here’s a case study showing how big jumps in Hispanic turnout aren’t automatic
title_en:
Things are different in 2026 vs 2020, but here’s a case study showing how big jumps in Hispanic turnout aren’t automatically good for Dems in Texas.

In 2016, Hillary Clinton won Starr County by 60 (!) points. In 2020, turnout there surged by over 50%. However, it was Trump who effectively gained 100% of the vote increase.
title_zh:
2026 年与 2020 年的情况有所不同，但这里有一个案例研究，显示拉美裔投票率的大幅跃升并不自动对德克萨斯州的民主党有利。

2016 年，希拉里·克林顿 (Hillary Clinton) 以 60 (!) 个百分点赢得斯塔尔县。 2
full_text_en:
Things are different in 2026 vs 2020, but here’s a case study showing how big jumps in Hispanic turnout aren’t automatically good for Dems in Texas.

In 2016, Hillary Clinton won Starr County by 60 (!) points. In 2020, turnout there surged by over 50%. However, it was Trump who effectively gained 100% of the vote increase.
full_text_zh:
2026 年与 2020 年的情况有所不同，但这里有一个案例研究，显示拉美裔投票率的大幅跃升并不自动对德克萨斯州的民主党有利。

2016 年，希拉里·克林顿 (Hillary Clinton) 以 60 (!) 个百分点赢得斯塔尔县。 2020年，那里的投票率飙升了50%以上。然而，特朗普实际上获得了100%的选票增长。
